items.title: Molecular Origins of Site-Specific CO2 Absorption in Hydrated Deep Eutectic Solvents
items.abstract: Deep eutectic solvents (DESs) have emerged as promising candidates for CO 2 capture because of their highly tunable structures and CO 2 absorption capacities. However, their behavior under practical operating conditions remains poorly understood. In particular, the effect of water on DES structure and their CO 2 absorption capacity remains unclear. In this work, we use free energy perturbation (FEP) and molecular simulations to determine the CO 2 absorption capacities and transport properties of hydrated hydrophilic and hydrophobic DESs. Our results show that increasing water concentration decreases viscosity but also makes CO 2 solvation less favorable in both DESs, revealing a trade-off between transport properties and CO 2 absorption capacity. This trade-off is more favorable for the hydrophobic DES, which shows a substantial reduction in viscosity while maintaining a negative CO 2 solvation free energy. In contrast, the solvation free energy of the hydrophilic DES increases more substantially, becoming positive at 15 wt% H 2 O. items.abstract: A comprehensive understanding of the microscopic processes governing ion transport in concentrated electrolyte solutions is essential for developing efficient, water-based batteries and energy storage devices. LiTFSI has emerged as a model system for Waterin-Salt (WiS) electrolytes because it can be investigated over a wide concentration range. Here, we combine Raman and THz spectroscopy with classical MD simulations to elucidate the reorganization of the water network across concentrations ranging from 1 to 21 mol·kg-1. Isotopic substitution of H2O by D2O allows us to disentangle the distinct spectroscopic contributions of ion rattling modes and H-bond motifs in the THz frequency range. The analysis reveals two solvent-dependent modes in the region of the translational and librational water network modes, rationalized as an overall strengthening of directional H-bonds and a decrease in orientational preference. items.title: Systematic Bias in TD-DFT Absorption Predictions for Nucleic Acid Fluorophores
items.abstract: Fluorescent nucleic-acid reporters are central to sequence-specific sensing and imaging, making reliable prediction of the absorption maximum () an important design objective. Due to the potential accelerated design of new reporters using computational methods, the present work benchmarks the performance of time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) against experimental values for a database of 116 chromophores that span literature-validated fluorescent nucleobase analogues and other small molecule probes. Three methodological variables are systematically examined: 1) the relationship between linear-response TD-DFT and the Tamm–Dancoff approximation (TDA), 2) basis-set convergence from double- through quadruple- quality with and without diffuse augmentation for two different families, and 3) the performance of 63 density functionals distributed across Jacob’s ladder. values computed with TDA are found to differ from full TD-DFT results by relatively small, systematic shifts and exhibit a near-linear relationship to the full response treatment, enabling straightforward post hoc calibration while retaining substantial gains in computational efficiency and numerical robustness.

items.abstract: 2,3- and 2,4-Disubstituted 2-azabicyclo[3.n.1]alkanes (n = 1, 2) are introduced as bioisosteres of 1,2- and 1,3-disubstituted piperidines, respectively. The 2-azabicyclo[3.1.1]heptane and 2-azabicyclo[3.2.1]octane cores were constructed in a single step by a scalable intramolecular carbene N–H insertion, with subsequent functionalization giving α- and β-amino acids and other bifunctional derivatives amenable to two-point diversification. Structural analysis of the disubstituted 2-azabicyclo[3.1.1]heptane derivatives showed that both substitution patterns matched their reference piperidines in all exit vector parameters but one, and in that one occupied a geometry not observed for the parent ring. Virtual decoration of the functional groups on both 2-azabicyclo[3.n.1]alkane cores gave a library whose calculated physicochemical property profile coincided with that of the monocyclic reference, except for a modest increase in molecular weight. To validate the bioisosteric replacement in a biological context, conformationally restricted bupivacaine analogs based on both cores were prepared and evaluated in the mouse tail-flick assay. items.title: A benchmark dataset of 86 intermolecular interactions of neutrals, ions, radicals and radical ions with water and hydrogen sulfide
items.abstract: Guiding the selection of modern density functional approximations (DFAs) for intermolecular interactions requires diverse benchmark assessments. This work reports the development of a new test set of 86 binary complexes formed between either H 2 O or H 2 S and 31 selected partner species, comprising 15 neutral closed-shell molecules, 7 neutral radicals, 4 closed-shell anions, 2 closed-shell cations, and 3 cation radicals. The radical complexes are susceptible to delocalization error, while the interaction strengths span weak to very strong. Benchmark results are obtained at the coupled cluster singles, doubles and perturbative triples, CCSD(T), level, extrapolated towards the complete basis set limit from augmented triple and quadruple zeta basis calculations. In common with other benchmarks, we find that the best functional on each higher rung of Jacob’s Ladder improves over the rung below, consistent with the potential to reduce the delocalization error. items.abstract: Interaction of cold plasma with aqueous media underpins emerging technologies in water treatment, chemical conversion, and biomedicine, yet scalable plasma-liquid activation remains limited by inefficient gas-liquid mass transfer and rapid reactive-species decay. items.abstract: Addressing urban air pollution requires identifying, quantifying, and mitigating emission sources, yet bottom-up inventories often lack fine spatiotemporal precision and rarely capture unpermitted or informally operated sources. items.title: QEpy: Quantum ESPRESSO in Python
items.abstract: QEpy is a Python electronic-structure software package based on Quantum ESPRESSO (QE). QEpy accomplishes two goals. First, it simplifies running and prototyping calculations with QE. Second, it targets nonstandard workflows where the electronic-structure engine is used in ways for which it was not originally designed. For example, QEpy can instruct QE to run with custom potentials in the Hamiltonian, including external, exchange-correlation, and local pseudopotentials. QEpy also exposes, at any point during an electronic-structure calculation, including between self-consistent-field cycles, quantities that would normally be accessible only through post-processing, such as the electron density and wavefunctions. QEpy’s API to the Atomic Simulation Environment (ASE) gives direct access to ASE-based workflows and tools. These capabilities make QEpy a flexible platform for implementing custom workflows, interfacing QE with other simulation tools, and prototyping new electronic-structure methods. items.title: Transfer learning guides discovery of NIR-emissive DNA-stabilized silver nanoclusters
items.abstract: Water-soluble near-infrared (NIR) emitters are of interest for imaging in the tissue transparency window. DNA-stabilized silver nanoclusters (DNA-AgN) hold promise for this spectral window, but it remains challenging to select oligonucleotides that stabilize NIR-emitting DNA-AgN. We address this challenge using transfer learning (TL), constructing a model that learns from experimental data for DNA-AgN stabilized by short 10-base oligonucleotides to then design longer oligonucleotides for larger, NIR-emitting nanoclusters. Using this model, we experimentally uncover 321 new DNA-AgN with peak emission beyond 800 nm, increasing design success by 710%. DNA-AgN designed using TL exhibit favorable properties including substantial emission above 1,000 nm, high fluorescence quantum yield, upconversion fluorescence, and a 14-electron count - the highest reported for DNA-AgN. These results demonstrate the power of TL for extracting physiochemical information from a limited parameter space and extrapolating these principles for broader design challenges, which is especially important when training data is scarce.

Though conceptualized in the 1930s, market adoption of HyDR remains limited due to reactor failures from sticking of iron-ore pellets. We found that tumor-specific, HPV-human DNA junctions are detectable in serum cell-free DNA of a fraction of cervical cancer patients at the time of initial treatment and/or at 6 months following treatment. Retrospective analysis revealed these junctions were more frequently detectable in women in whom the cancer later recurred. We also found that cervical cancers caused by HPV types outside of phylogenetic clade α9 had a higher recurrence frequency than those caused by α9 types in both our study and The Cancer Genome Atlas cervical cancer database, despite the higher prevalence ofα9 types, including HPV16, in cervical cancer. Thus, HPV-human DNA junction detection in serum cell-free DNA and HPV type determination in tumor tissue may help predict recurrence risk. Screening serum cell-free DNA for junctions may also offer an unambiguous non-invasive means to monitor absence of recurrence following treatment.

items.abstract: From idea generation to testing, drug discovery is a lengthy and expensive process. Rather than chasing all of their molecule ideas, scientists prioritize certain molecules that are more likely to be successful, from synthesis to safety to therapeutic use. Machine learning and AI enable researchers to narrow their candidate choices by predicting important properties such as ADMET (Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, and Toxicity). This study uses the Plasma Protein Binding (PPB) dataset from DeepChem’s MoleculeNet, with several graph neural networks (GNNs), ChemBERTa (a language model for SMILES strings of molecules), and fusions of these models. The performance of these neural models is compared against two standard tree-based models: Random Forest (RF) and XGBoost. Instead of random splitting of the dataset, this study evaluates the models based on scaffold splitting that separates molecules by the Bemis–Murcko scaffold and puts the entire group into only the training, validation, or test set. items.title: Cationic Selenuranes Enable Direct Linchpin Formation in Arenes
items.abstract: The formation of linchpins is a powerful strategy for increasing molecular complexity. Chalcogenonium salts have become valuable intermediates for molecular diversification, owing to their exceptional chemoselectivity in arene C–H functionalization and a synthetic versatility comparable to that of halides and pseudohalides. Sulfonium group introduction through an isohypsic process from S(IV) precursors requires activation with strong acids or anhydrides. Here, we report the direct synthesis of selenonium salts from bench-stable Se(III) cationic selenuranes using a simple dump-and-stir protocol. The transformation proceeds under air at ambient temperature and requires no exogenous activators. Mechanistic investigations reveal high sensitivity to electronic effects (ρ = −10), whereas site selectivity is determined by the rate-limiting deprotonation step (kH/kD = 2.3). The method is scalable to 10.0 mmol ( 6.2 g) and provides direct access to selenonium salts derived from complex molecules. The resulting selenonium salts serve as versatile linchpins for photochemical, nucleophilic, and transition-metal-catalyzed transformations, enabling late-stage molecular diversification.

Here, we present ReCoFlow, a novel trajectorylikelihood-free reinforcement learning framework for reward-contrastive post-training of pretrained molecular flow-matching models. Within ReCoFlow, reward-favored molecules provide positive endpoint supervision for the flow-matching model, whereas reward-disfavored molecules are used to construct reference-guided negative targets. The resulting models reproduce available experimental thermodynamic and structural data, and spontaneously develop microphase separated morphologies consistent with experimental observations. items.title: Data-driven strategies for enzyme engineering: From machine learning to protein language models
items.abstract: Enzymes are key biocatalysts that drive diverse biological processes and industrial applications, offering sustainable alternatives to conventional chemical catalysis. However, the enormous enzyme sequence space and the limited functional annotation have created an urgent demand for computational approaches to accelerate enzyme discovery and engineering. Recent advances in computational methods are accelerating enzyme engineering from empirical trial and error toward predictive design. This review summarizes representative computational tools and predictive models in the enzyme engineering workflow, including (1) enzyme data resources, (2) functional enzyme discovery, (3) enzyme property prediction (e.g., kinetics, optimal temperature and PH, solubility, promiscuity, and specificity), (4) de novo enzyme design, and (5) computationally guided enzyme optimization. We further compare current computational strategies, discuss their strengths and limitations in different engineering scenarios, and highlight emerging trends toward foundation models, generative artificial intelligence, multimodal learning, and closed-loop design–build–test–learn platforms.

items.abstract: Engineering the spatial organization of proteins offers a powerful strategy for controlling biochemical reactions and material properties in synthetic cells. However, dynamically organizing multiple proteins at the nanometer scale remains challenging. We developed asymmetric lipid–oleosin hybrid vesicles in which engineered oleosin molecules served as membrane-forming scaffolds with two orthogonal conjugation systems. External chemical stimuli rapidly recruited two distinct proteins to individual oleosin molecules, generating persistent nanometer-scale proximity, as demonstrated by single-molecule tracking. In an alditol oxidase–horseradish peroxidase cascade, organization of both enzymes on the same oleosin scaffold enhanced product formation compared with intermolecular membrane recruitment. This localized cascade further drove stimulus-responsive polymerization to form membrane-associated cytoskeleton-like structures, increasing vesicle resistance to hypertonic stress. This programmable membrane scaffold couples external signals with molecular organization, enhanced biochemical reactions, and membrane mechanics, providing a framework for engineering synthetic cells that convert
items.authors: Masato Suzuki, Rinshi S. Kasai, Koki Kamiya

items.title: Finite-Field Second Hyperpolarizability via Adaptive Bayesian Quantum Phase Estimation for Early Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computers: Ground-State Energies Beyond Chemical Accuracy
items.abstract: The static second hyperpolarizability governs third-order nonlinear-optical responses but is difficult to compute by first-principles methods because finite-field extraction requires a fourth-order energy derivative. The resulting error amplification demands sub-µHa ground-state energies, far beyond conventional chemical accuracy. Standard multi-qubit QPE can in principle meet this precision but requires a wide ancilla register, while single-ancilla iterative QPE (IQPE) is limited by a binary-grid quantization floor. We develop an adaptive Bayesian QPE (BQPE) workflow that uses a single ancilla, terminal measurements, and real-time classical feedback to estimate the eigenphase through a continuous posterior rather than a fixed binary grid. For a linear H4 chain in the STO-3G basis, represented by a six-qubit parity Hamiltonian with one ancilla, BQPE reaches a ground-state energy error of ≈ 10−7 Ha at controlled-U depth mmax ≈ 215, about two orders of magnitude below the IQPE floor. items.authors: Katsuki Okuno

items.title: Catalytic Phosphorus-Based Hydrogen Atom
items.abstract: We report the first catalytic phosphorus-based hydrogen atom transfer system. Using an iridium photocatalyst and 10 mol% diphenylphosphine sulfide, we achieve decarboxylative reduction of diverse carboxylic acids—including peptides and pharmaceuticals—to C–H products in up to 95% yield, without stoichiometric reductants. Mechanistic studies reveal an unprecedented anionic relay: a phosphoryl radical is reduced to a phosphinoyl anion, which upon protonation regenerates the P–H catalyst. This work establishes catalytic turnover in phosphorus-based HAT and identifies a new elementary step in main-group radical chemistry.
items.authors: Pratik Avinash, Kayla Merrigan, Bartosz Bieszczad

items.title: Vicem: Automating Molecular Mechanics Modeling of Solvation Dynamics with Applications to Time-Resolved X-ray Scattering
items.abstract: Time-resolved X-ray solution scattering (trXSS) probes molecular-scale structural dynamics in solution, but its interpretation requires efficient computational methodologies and models for assessing how changes in solute structure and charge distribution affect the surrounding solvent shell and the resulting scattering signal. We present VICEM, an OpenMM/ASE-based software suite for constructing solvated molecular models, running molecular dynamics simulations, inspecting and analyzing the resulting trajectories, while exposing solute geometry, partial charges, Lennard–Jones parameters, and bonded terms as editable variables for model refinement. VICEM includes an approximate restrained-solute model designed for rapid solvent-shell sampling around prescribed solute geometries, together with utilities for correcting the potential energy along selected intramolecular coordinates. We benchmark the restrained model against established force fields for 244 systems comprising neutral organic molecules, charged organic solutes, and transition-metal complexes. items.title: The Gated Quantum Resonator: a reduced-representation Hamiltonian–network framework for gated driven–dissipative quantum systems
items.abstract: High-dimensional driven–dissipative systems are often described either microscopically or through reduced models whose relation to the underlying dynamics is unclear. Originally motivated by geometrygated catalytic and enzymatic dynamics, the construction is developed here independently of any particular molecular application. We formulate the Gated Quantum Resonator (GQR) as a controlled reducedrepresentation framework in which selected coherent coordinates are modulated by structural or environmental gates. The retained coordinates are supplied by an upstream modelling step; no projection or truncation algorithm is introduced. From a gate-dependent Hamiltonian we develop complementary mode, network and port–Hamiltonian representations, distinguishing exact preservation properties from phenomenological closures requiring independent validation. Open-system dynamics are introduced through a GKSL generator. For the linear lossless sector, the specified mechanical–network map exactly preserves normal-mode frequencies and modal eigenspaces, while matched input–output equality is a consistency property by construction. items.title: Accelerating the Design of New Natural Deep Eutectic Solvents with Supervised Variational Autoencoders
items.abstract: The rational design of natural deep eutectic solvents (NaDESs) is hindered by the vast combinatorial space arising from the possible combinations of hydrogen bond donors and acceptors. This enormous design space limits the systematic experimental exploration of their physicochemical properties. In this work, we propose a supervised variational autoencoder (SVAE) framework to efficiently explore this chemical space by coupling generative modeling with property prediction. The model is trained on a curated dataset of deep eutectic solvents to learn simultaneously the latent structural representations and correlations with target properties, including melting point, density, and viscosity. The SVAE generates virtual NaDES candidates characterized by molecular descriptors, component ratios, and target property values. To associate these virtual candidates with real molecules, a descriptor matching strategy is applied using the COCONUT natural product database. The resulting NaDES candidates are subsequently validated using predictive models trained on experimental DES data. items.title: From Materials to Metalloenzymes: Superconducting Microresonators for Characterization of Thin Films
items.abstract: Electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy is a widely used technique for the characterization of paramagnetic centers across a wide range of disciplines. Yet, the detection limits of conventional 3D microwave resonators hinder the application of EPR to nanoscale and magnetically dilute thin films relevant to quantum, catalytic and biological devices. Here we show that high temperature superconducting spiral microresonators fabricated from YBa2Cu3O7-x enable pulse EPR measurements on diverse thin films with a sensitivity improvement of two to three orders of magnitude over commercial resonators. Templated 50 nm films of copper phthalocyanine (CuPc) diluted in metal-free phthalocyanine (H2Pc) deposited onto the microresonator were detectable in echo-detected EPR field sweeps with the templating effect clearly visible from narrowing of the spectrum compared to powder samples. The number of Cu(II) spins present in a single thin film of CuPc on a microresonator with 400 μm diameter was ~1011, as determined by measurement of coherence memory times (Tm) and longitudinal (T1) spin relaxation times. items.title: Advancement of triphos-Ru catalyzed C–O bond disconnections and its challenges
items.abstract: Cured epoxy resins are crosslinked thermoset materials with applications including carbon-or glass-reinforced composites, but whose extensive C–O and C–N bond networks renders recycling challenging. Previously, our group has reported a Ru-triphos-catalyzed system for the chemical deconstruction of amine-cured epoxy resins, enabling recovery of bisphenol A (BPA) under relatively mild conditions. Subsequent mechanistic studies identified slow catalyst activation and catalyst deactivation as key limitations. Herein, these insights were used to develop improved catalytic systems through pre-catalyst and reaction design. Replacement of the original triphos-Ru-TMM pre-catalyst enabled improved catalytic performance, while ligand design enabled the use of H2, instead of isopropanol, as reductant. Despite these advances, the improved performance observed for model compounds did not translate directly to cured epoxy resins. Reaction optimization revealed pronounced dependencies on substrate concentration, and polymer accessibility, while computational studies suggest changes in catalyst speciation imposed by conformational constraints. items.title: Machine learning-accelerated evolutionary Monte Carlo for rapid phase exploration of compositionally complex materials in reactive environments
items.abstract: Compositionally complex materials, e.g. high-entropy alloys/oxides, have long been of research interest for their unique mechanical and functional properties thanks to the synergistic effects between the large number of components. More recently, they have emerged as a promising platform for the development of novel heterogeneous catalysts for thermo- and electro-chemical applications. However, computational investigation of the phase stability of such catalyst materials remains challenging due to the large design space and the complex active site dynamics under reaction conditions. In this paper, we present a novel evolutionary Monte Carlo algorithm which allows fast exploration of stable compositionally-complex catalyst phases in reactive environments and can be generalized for any catalyst materials and any reaction conditions. In detail, we will showcase that this method can be used in combination with finetuned machine learning potentials for predicting bulk and surface mixing/segregating behaviors of compositionally-complex catalysts under various reaction conditions with reasonable computational cost.

items.title: THIOETHERS AS POTENTIAL ANTIBACTERIAL AGENTS AGAINST METHICILLIN-RESISTANT STAPHYLOCOCCUS AUREUS (MRSA)
items.abstract: The emergence and rapid spread of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) have created an urgent need for new antibacterial agents capable of overcoming established resistance mechanisms. Among the diverse sulfur-containing scaffolds, thioethers have attracted increasing attention because of their structural versatility and ability to modulate antibacterial activity through incorporation into different pharmacophores. This review provides a comprehensive overview of synthetic, semisynthetic, and natural or natural-product-derived thioether compounds evaluated against MRSA, with emphasis on their structural features, structure-activity relationships (SAR), antibacterial potency, and mechanisms of action. The major classes discussed include aminoglycoside-derived thioether amphiphiles, membrane-active small-molecule thioethers, quinazolinone and quinoline thioether scaffolds, pleuromutilin thioether derivatives, SecA-targeting thioethers, chalcone and oxazolidinone derivatives, FtsZ-targeting thioethers, anti-virulence and antibiofilm agents, antimicrobial peptidomimetics, and natural-product-derived thioether compounds. items.title: Chemoproteomic mapping of active glycan-processing networks in a defined gut microbiome
items.abstract: Microbiome studies typically infer function from gene content or expression, but these measurements do not establish which enzymes are catalytically active or what substrates they recognise. Here we use a multiplexed panel of mechanism-based glycosidase probes to map active glycan-processing enzymes directly from caecal samples of mice colonised with a defined, 14-member, human gut microbiota. Activity-based protein profiling identifies host and microbial enzymes involved in starch, β-glucan, xyloglucan and xylan degradation and links them to defined taxa and loci. Decorated probes resolve branch and substitution preferences within active enzyme families, revealing xylanase activities poorly detected by bulk substrate assays. Several prominent activities are assigned to low-abundance Bacteroides species, while enzyme deployment differs among animals sharing a common inoculum and diet. These results establish activity-based chemoproteomics as a complementary layer to metagenomics, transcriptomics and proteomics for defining functional glycan-processing states in host-associated microbiomes.
items.authors: Isabelle B. Pickles, Thamy L. R. Corrêa, Qinnan Yang, Yurong Chen, Zirui Li, Nicole M. Koropatkin

items.title: alchemy: systematic enumeration and thermodynamic screening of small-molecule radical reaction networks
items.abstract: Automated construction of chemical reaction networks is limited by the combinatorial growth of possible molecules, intermediates, and formal transformations. We present alchemy, an open-source Python workflow for systematic enumeration and screening of small-molecule radical reaction networks. Within an explicitly bounded graph space, alchemy generates connected, neutral C/N/H molecular graphs with single, double, or triple bonds and specified radical counts; RDKit sanitisation and canonicalisation then remove graph-invalid and duplicate records. Reaction candidates are constructed without learned reaction templates by combining bond-dissociation records into rearrangement and transfer stoichiometries. Parallel generation, disk-backed storage, machine-learning prediction of molecular Gibbs free energies, and Kuzu graph representation make the resulting formal network searchable. In a trimethylamine case study limited to at most five heavy atoms and one unpaired electron per reaction side, the workflow generated 41,735 unique molecular graphs and 60,035 first-generation radical-transfer records. items.title: Directed Evolution of a Non-Heme Iron Enzyme for Enantioselective Dearomative Nitrene Transfer: Synthesis of 3a-Aminopyrroloindoline Alkaloids
items.abstract: Enzymatic nitrene-induced dearomatization represents an unexplored area of biocatalytic reactivity. Here, we report the directed evolution of AsqJ, a non-heme iron enzyme from aspoquinolone biosynthesis, to catalyze the first biocatalytic asymmetric dearomative nitrene transfer into indoles to furnish enantioenriched 3a-aminopyrroloindolines — a privileged scaffold in bioactive indole alkaloid natural products. Obtained through iterative semi-rational engineering and structure-informed mutagenesis, the final variant achieves up to 98% yield and 99% ee. The reaction accommodates a range of indole substrates, affording up to 86% isolated yield on preparative scale with consistently high enantioselectivity. Molecular dynamics simulations suggest that directed evolution established a new substrate-binding conformation that is distinct from the starting variant through a reorganized hydrogen-bonding network within a more preorganized active site. The synthetic utility of this platform is demonstrated through the total syntheses of two natural products, (+)-psychotriasine and (+)-psychotrimine. This work establishes asymmetric dearomative nitrene transfer as a new biocatalytic modality,

items.title: Entropy-Guided Dataset Reduction for Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials
items.abstract: Machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) deliver near-quantum-mechanical accuracy at a fraction of the computational cost. Their performance depends on the quality and composition of the training data: the training set must cover the range of atomic environments the model will encounter, yet unnecessary redundancy increases training cost without improving accuracy and can inadvertently introduce training biases. Dataset pruning (i.e., selecting a compact, representative subset from a larger collection) has emerged as a practical strategy for building high-quality training sets. Recently, methods based on informationtheoretic diversity measures such as QUESTS (Quick Uncertainty and Entropy from STructural Similarity) have shown significant promise, however, QUESTS requires specification of a lengthscale parameter (kernel bandwidth) that controls how similar two atomic environments must be before one is considered redundant. We show that operationally useful values of this parameter vary across structurally distinct phases, making naive automated pruning of heterogeneous datasets challenging. items.title: Applicability-Domain-Aware Evaluation of Machine-Learning NMR Chemical-Shift Prediction in Small drug Molecules: GT-NMR for 13C and CASCADE for 1H

items.title: Chemical Accuracy for Carbapenem Breakdown by Class A beta-Lactamases Using a Transferable Embedded Machine-Learned Potential
items.abstract: Bacterial resistance to carbapenems (potent β-lactam antibiotics) is a critical global health threat. The primary cause is β-lactamase enzymes that hydrolyze antibiotics. Previously, carbapenems resisted breakdown, making them ‘last resort’ antibiotics, but enzymes with carbapenemase activity have become widespread. Understanding and predicting the activity of β-lactamases will help in developing antibiotics and inhibitors, and combating antibiotic resistance. Effective prediction requires methods that are both accurate and computationally efficient. Multiscale combined quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) molecular dynamics simulations of reactions can discriminate between class A β-lactamases (the most widely distributed group) with or without carbapenemase activity, and identify determinants of activity. but face an accuracy/efficiency tradeoff: approximate semiempirical QM methods do not predict reaction barriers accurately, but higher level QM calculations require extensive computer time and resources, making them impractical for rapid predictions. items.title: An Attention-based Architecture to Decode Chemical Transformations from Process Spectroscopic Data
items.abstract: Spectroscopy is a powerful analytical technique that promises precise characterization of chemical species and their transformations in dynamic chemical processes. Traditionally, spectral signatures are interpreted by calibrating against established spectral libraries. However, for complex molecular systems, mixtures of multiple interacting compounds, or dynamical processes, the resulting spectral signals become highly convoluted. Conventional deconvolution based methods rely on the availability of prior information to effectively decompose the measured data into latent components and infer chemical transformations using plausible reaction templates. However, the dynamics, scale, and dimensionality of process spectroscopic data make such deconvolutions increasingly difficult and often ill-conditioned. These limitations are particularly pronounced in industrial process settings, thus reducing their effectiveness for quality control, impurity detection, and reaction pathway identification. items.title: Hypermolecule: Chemically Synthesized Three-dimensional Macroscopic Molecular Moiré Superlattices
items.abstract: Recently, moiré superlattices in two-dimensional (2D) systems have attracted significant attention owing to their tunable optical, electronic and quantum properties. Nevertheless, the studies of moiré systems were mostly limited to 2D systems, which make scalability and reproducibility an important issue. Here, we report evidence for the formation of moleculebased macroscopic three-dimensional (3D) moiré superlattice superstructure. We define the isolated 3D assembly as a hypermolecule that has no known natural or synthetic molecular analogue. The time-dependent evolution of the 2D moiré assemblies was investigated using transmission electron microscopy, UV-visible spectroscopy and photoluminescence studies, revealing the hierarchical progression of twist-stacked 2D moiré superlattices towards the growth of macroscopic moiré systems. In addition, X-ray diffraction characterization methods were pursued to elucidate the structural characteristics of the resulting 3D assemblies and establish the correlation between the 2D and 3D superlattices. items.title: Bridging MS2 Spectra and Chemical Space: Advances in Spectral Similarity, Molecular Retrieval, and De Novo Structure Discovery
items.abstract: Mass spectrometry-based metabolomics increasingly relies on computational methods to translate information-rich MS/MS fragmentation patterns into chemical insight, yet assigning chemical identities to spectra ("annotation") remains a major bottleneck because reference libraries cover only a small fraction of plausible compounds. In this review, we frame the field through the lens of two interacting representation spaces: spectral space, where MS/MS data reside, and chemical space, where molecules are represented by fingerprints, descriptors, or learned embeddings. We discuss how different design choices induce different geometries, what it means for spectra or molecules to be "close", and survey methods for representing and comparing spectra, representing molecules, and mapping between both spaces. We highlight emerging deep-learning trends for cross-modal alignment and retrieval, and we outline where the analogy to text-image learning breaks due to peak ambiguity, noise, and the one-to-many nature of spectrum-to-structure relationships.
items.authors: Julian Pollmann, Roman Bushuiev, Anton Bushuiev, Tomáš Pluskal, Florian Huber

items.title: Magnetic anisotropy of tellurium(I) and selenium(I)† in a Li3N host crystal
items.abstract: Magnetic anisotropy in low-coordinate main-group compounds has recently emerged as a promising route toward realizing single-molecule magnet behavior beyond traditional transition-metal and lanthanide systems. In this work, we investigate the electronic structure and magnetic properties of selenium-and tellurium-doped Li3N crystals using a combination of periodic density functional theory and embedded ionic-crystal QM/MM multireference calculations. Substitution of Li(1) sites by Se(I) and Te(I) generates low-coordinate np3 configurations embedded in a highly symmetric crystalline environment. Periodic calculations reveal substantial differences in spin localization and covalency between the two dopants: Te-doping stabilizes a spin-polarized electronic structure with localized magnetic character, whereas stronger Se 4p–N 2p hybridization leads to increased delocalization and a non-magnetic DFT ground state. items.title: From Proteins and Molecules to Cats and Dogs: Visualization as Scalable Minimum Spanning Trees
items.abstract: Dimensionality reduction and data visualization are essential for analyzing highdimensional datasets, yet traditional projection methods obscure local structural relationships. We present TMAP2, a scalable rewrite of TMAP that maps highdimensional data as a minimum spanning tree. TMAP2 accepts diverse input types, including continuous embeddings, sparse fingerprints, and precomputed graphs, and applies to single-cell, image, chemistry, or protein-language-model data. Every line on the map is therefore a real nearest-neighbor relationship, and exactly one path joins any two points. The number of edges along that path, its hop count, works as a coordinate along a progression: it recovers a pancreatic cell’s developmental age (Spearman 0.90), tracks the collection date of a SARS-CoV-2 spike sequence built from raw sequence alone (Spearman 0.86), and traces a smooth morph from a Persian cat to a Yorkshire terrier that crosses species at a single edge. On 3.6 million CAZyme sequences the same tree separates taxonomic domains and, within the family GH43, sorts sequences by catalytic activity, revealing an anchor enzyme annotated as one activity sitting among a cluster of another. items.title: Decoupling Morphological and Electronic Effects of Ni-Doped Ruthenium Oxide Oxygen Evolution Catalysts for PEM Water Electrolysis
items.abstract: Proper assessment of oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalyst performance requires recognising that doping can introduce simultaneous changes to structure, morphology, and electronic properties that together influence the observed electrochemical behaviour. In this study, Ni-doped RuO2 is used as a model system to systematically investigate how dopant concentration and synthesis temperature affect catalyst morphology and electronic structure. These trends are correlated with OER mass activity (MA), intrinsic activity, and stability enabling the morphological and intrinsic electronic contributions to catalyst performance to be distinguished. The acid-stable limit for bulk Ni incorporation in RuO2 is found to be approximately 10 mol%. Ni incorporation affects the rutile structure and inhibits particle growth, while lower synthesis temperatures decrease particle size. The best-performing Ni-doped RuO2 catalyst here shows up to a tenfold increase in OER MA compared with undoped RuO2. Surface area-based normalisation of MA reveals that this enhancement is partly caused by increased accessible surface area and includes an additional contribution from increased intrinsic OER activity. items.title: Simulation of Ultrafast Fe(II) Photoswitching Dynamics Triggered by Excitation within the Quintet Manifold
items.abstract: The quintet-to-singlet back-switching process in [Fe(tpy)2]2+(tpy=2,2’:6’,2"-terpyridine), [Fe(dftpy)2]2+ (dftpy=6,6"-difluoro-2,2’:6’,2"-terpyridine) and [Fe(dctpy)2]2+(dctpy=6,6"-dichloro-2,2’:6’,2"-terpyridine), together with the photorelaxation dynamics of the [Fe(dftpy)2]2+ spin-crossover and the [Fe(dctpy)2]2+ high-spin complexes were investigated by full-dimensional trajectory surface hopping (TSH) dynamics. Following photoexcitation, the initial population of the 5Eg (5MC) state decays quickly via a branching mechanism of direct (5Eg → 5T2g) and 3MC-crossed (5Eg → 3MC→5T2g) processes, with the latter dominating the dynamics. The quintet-to-singlet photoconversion, the key step of the back-switching process, remains inefficient ( 10%). This low efficiency arises because the singlet–triplet–quintet crossing region is readily accessible only during the initial sub-picosecond dynamics ( 500 fs). Shifting the crossing region to improve its accessibility could substantially enhance the quintet-to-singlet conversion efficiency, suggesting that more extensive chemical modification could significantly optimize the back-switching process. items.title: Synthesis, Spectroscopic Characterisation, and Structural Elucidation of Ni(II) and Cu(II) Complexes of a Novel N,N’-Diaminophthalamidoxime Ligand
items.abstract: A new N,N’-diaminophthalamidoxime (NAD) ligand was synthesised by reacting hydrazine hydrate with diethyl phthalate to give phthalic dihydrazide, which was subsequently reacted with hydroxylamine to yield the target ligand. The ligand was reacted with Ni(II) and Cu(II) salts to give [Ni(NAD)2]Cl2 and [Cu(NAD)2(OAc)2], respectively. The ligand and its complexes were characterised by solubility studies, melting point determination, complexometric metal analysis, room-temperature magnetic susceptibility, and infrared and UV–Visible spectroscopy. The free ligand was soluble in DMSO, DMF and hot ethanol, but insoluble in chloroform, ethyl acetate, acetone, methanol, dichloromethane and distilled water, and all three compounds showed high thermal stability ( 300 °C). Diagnostic infrared bands at 3572 and 3524 cm-1 (νNH2 and νOH) and UV bands at 48,300, 36,630 and 28,985 cm-1 (n→σ*, π→π* and n→π*, respectively) confirmed the identity of the free ligand. Complexometric titration gave experimental metal contents of 9.92% (Cu) and 9.82% (Ni), in good agreement with the theoretical values of 10.09% and 10.15%, consistent with 1:2 metal-to-ligand stoichiometry in both complexes. items.title: Phase-Dependent Thermally Activated Self-Discharge of β-NiOOH and γ-NiOOH Electrodes
items.abstract: Nickel oxyhydroxide electrodes undergo spontaneous self-discharge that is strongly accelerated at elevated temperature. Although detrimental to alkaline batteries, this reaction is central to electrochemical–thermally activated chemical (E‑TAC) water splitting. The process operates in two distinct steps: electrochemical charging of Ni(OH)2 in cold (~25 °C) alkaline electrolyte and hydrogen generation at the cathode, followed by spontaneous regeneration of the charged NiOOH anode in hot (~80–100 °C) alkaline electrolyte, with concurrent oxygen evolution. A key unresolved question is how the charged-phase composition of NiOOH affects this thermally activated self-discharge. Here, we prepare phase-pure cobalt-doped β-NiOOH and γ-NiOOH electrodes using tailored electrochemical charging protocols and compare their short-term self-discharge in hot alkaline electrolyte simulating the TAC step in the E-TAC cycle. X-ray diffraction and iodometric titration show that phase-pure β-NiOOH undergoes little or no measurable structural or oxidation-state change after 5 min in 5 M KOH at 80 or 100 °C. items.authors: Elena Praznikov, Avigail Varveri Landman, Avner Rothschild

items.title: Temporally decoupled electrochemiluminescence breaks the sensitivity–portability tradeoff in water toxicity sensing
items.abstract: Multiple technologies have been developed to reconcile the trade-off between sensitivity and portability, which is a persistent fundamental challenge in chemical sensing. Among them, electrochemiluminescence (ECL) has the advantages of simple device configuration and outstanding sensitivity based on the transduction of electrochemical signals into optical readouts. However, this is based on multi-step interfacial electron transfer, wherein the concomitant efficiency losses and areadependent signal intensity inherently constitute the primary limitations. Herein, a novel photochargeable wireless ECL (PC-Wireless-ECL) system is established based on a bifunctional carbon nitride (CN). This strategy boosts the ECL signal intensity by eliminating the dependence on the electrode dimensions and decoupling the excitation and emission processes temporally. By constructing portable bifunctional CN vials coupled with a miniaturized light intensity sensor, this system revolutionizes the conventional ECL measurement paradigm and realizes on-site, rapid, and highly sensitive screening of water toxicity, thereby offering a new strategy for next-generation in-field analytical technologies.
items.authors: Chuan Huang, Dan Han, Hong Yang, Kaiqing Wu, Yanfei Shen, Rong Jin

items.title: Polyelectrolyte Solutes, Gels, and Coacervates Differentially Impact Proto-Metabolic Ni-Catalyzed Bicarbonate Reduction.
items.abstract: Reactions using metal and mineral catalysis likely provided vital organic feedstocks for the process of life’s origination, accessing early metabolic pathways, building proto-metabolism, and providing avenues for compartmentalization. Towards proto-cellular encapsulation, a growing pool of multiply-charged solutes and polymers, as well as organic-rich phases, would have influenced the operation of Earth’s proto-metabolic pathways. Here, we employ quantitative NMR and model molecules containing relevant carboxylate, amine, and phosphate moieties to describe their effect on the catalytic reduction of bicarbonate to formate, the first step in ancient carbon fixation, such as via a precursor reductive Acetyl-CoA (Wood-Ljungdahl) pathway or reductive tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle. We find that this proto-metabolic carbon fixation process is relatively robust to build-up of organics, maintaining yields within about twofold despite relatively high concentrations of organic additives. Solute effects are not simply predicted by charge or solute size but depend on adsorption, participation in competing reactions, and solute-solute interactions. items.abstract: Machine-learning QSAR models can prioritize antioxidant compounds, but apparent accuracy depends strongly on how chemical data are partitioned for validation. This study develops a reproducible DPPH antioxidant QSAR workflow using 1,891 curated molecules from a public 30 min DPPH dataset. items.title: Engineering a Carboxylesterase for Acyl Transfer to Amines
items.abstract: Within the mechanistic realm of centralized catalysis (chemical catalysis), reactivity activation is site-centered on reactant functional groups and site-driven from catalytic centers, leading to a low-resolution catalytic architecture with low catalytic activity and catalytic efficiency. In contrast, within the mechanistic realm of decentralized catalysis (biological catalysis), reactivity activation is reactant-spanned on both functional groups and appendage groups and enclosure-driven from catalytic cavity, offering a high-resolution catalytic architecture with high catalytic activity and catalytic efficiency. Herein, as a proof-of-concept illustration for reactant-spanned and enclosure-driven enzymatic catalysis (as exemplary for biological catalysis), we report the engineering of a carboxylesterase for acyl transfer from carboxylesters to amines. The precision disjoint presentation activation of acyl group and amino group has empowered the achievement of an expansive reactant scope of both carboxylesters and amines. items.title: Unveiling the Potential of Biobased Bifuran unit in Conjugated Polymers: Synthesis, Thermal Properties, Photophysics, and Comparative Study with Phenylene and Thiophene Analogues for OLED Applications
items.abstract: The bifuran unit is an attractive biobased building block for organic electronics, however its potential in electroluminescent devices has not been explored. In this study, a series of bifuranbased conjugated polymers, PBFAr1–PBFAr9, was synthesized via Suzuki–Miyaura polycondensation to evaluate the effect of the bifuran unit on thermal, photophysical, and electrochemical properties. For comparison, analogous polymers containing phenylene (PSPhAr1), biphenyl (PBPhAr1), and bithiophene (PBTAr1) units were also synthesized. Characterization showed that the bifuran-containing polymers exhibit varied thermal stability, emission in both solution and the solid state. Specifically, the photoluminescence quantum yield of chloroform solution of PBFAr1 was 43%, which was higher than the 39% observed for the bithiophene-based analogue, PBTAr1. Kelvin probe measurements indicated an energy-level alignment with the ITO anode that may facilitate hole injection. Solution-processed OLEDs with an ITO/PEDOT:PSS/emissive polymer/LiF/Al architecture were fabricated, and the PBFAr1-based device exhibited bright cyan electroluminescence at 484 nm. items.title: A Distributed Diffusion Landscape Governs CO2 Coproduct Release from Fatty Acid Photodecarboxylase
items.abstract: The diffusion of small ligands within proteins is a fundamental yet poorly resolved step in enzymatic turnover.Recent studies have shown that ligand migration can involve networks of transient internal cavities and multiple competing exit routes, raising the question of whether such heterogeneity is a general feature of small-molecule egress.Here, we address this question in fatty acid photodecarboxylase (FAP), a light-driven enzyme that generates CO 2 as a small diffusive coproduct during fatty-acid decarboxylation.Using nine independent classical molecular dynamics simulations of Cv FAP, we show that CO 2 escapes the protein on the µs timescale with kinetics consistent with time-resolved infrared measurements, whereas the alkane product remains bound on the simulated timescale.Before release, CO 2 diffuses through a heterogeneous network of transient cavities, populating several distinct sites before escaping through multiple competing surface exit pathways rather than a single dominant route.One cavity positions CO 2 near C432, consistent with formation of the thiocarbonate intermediate previously identified.CO 2 release is likewise distributed among multiple surface exit points

items.title: The Role of In Situ Crosslinked Polysiloxane/Polylactide Micro-Networks on the PLA Brittle-Ductile Transition
items.abstract: Polylactide (PLA) has garnered significant attention as a potentially sustainable substitute for conventional petrochemical polymers. This attention is attributed to several factors, including its renewable origin, biodegradability, and its compatibility with conventional polymer processing techniques. However, its inherent fragility restricts its broader utilization as an engineering plastic. In this study, the investigation focused on the thermally activated reactive modification of PLA with two functional polysiloxanes of varying molecular architectures. This modification was explored as a toughening strategy, with the objective of promoting the brittle-to-ductile (BD) transition through the formation of a locally entangled polysiloxane/PLA micro-network within the PLA matrix. Extraction, thermal, spectroscopic, and morphological analyses were conducted to confirm the formation of a crosslinked phase. items.title: Interface-Engineered MXene/TMD Heterostructures for Efficient Hydrogen Evolution: Progress, DFT-Guided Mechanisms, and Perspectives
items.abstract: The hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) requires efficient, durable, and earth-abundant electrocatalysts to reduce reliance on platinum-group metals. MXene/transition-metal dichalcogenide (TMD) heterostructures offer a promising platform by combining the abundant, tunable catalytic sites of TMDs with the high electrical conductivity, hydrophilicity, and versatile surface chemistry of MXenes. This review critically examines recent advances in the synthesis, interfacial engineering, and HER performance of MXene/TMD heterostructures, with particular emphasis on how interfacial interactions govern catalytic behavior. The roles of phase engineering, defect and heteroatom incorporation, surface terminations, and heterointerface construction are discussed in relation to interfacial charge redistribution, electronic-structure modulation, hydrogen adsorption energetics, active-site accessibility, and reaction kinetics. Experimental HER performance across representative MXene/TMD systems is compared to establish structure-interface-performance relationships and identify the origins of enhanced activity and stability. items.title: Machine Learning Optimization of Polymeric Complex Coacervate Micelles Reveals Cell-Type-Specific Formulations for Enhanced mRNA Delivery
items.abstract: The cell-type dependent transfection heterogeneity of polymeric mRNA delivery remains a fundamental barrier to their broad translation. The field has historically addressed this by optimizing the cationic component itself, refining amine identity, density, and block architecture to maximize transfection. Even highly optimized cationic carriers, however, still transfect some cell types well and others poorly, because no single cation chemistry can simultaneously match the internalization and cytoplasmic trafficking biology of every target. Rather than seeking a universally optimal carrier chemistry, we instead sought a tunable formulation framework capable of adapting charge balance and interfacial properties across distinct cellular environments. Here, we report a multicomponent complex coacervate micelle platform in which a cationic oligoamine-functionalized A7 amphiphile , an anionic poly(carboxyethyl acrylate) (CEA) homopolymer, and a neutral-anionic poly(ethylene glycol)-b-poly(carboxyethyl acrylate) (PEG-CEA) diblock are co-assembled into a single carrier, with the anionic and stealth components associating electrostatically with the cationic micelle as external corona species

items.title: Melt-State Ligand Addition Generates a Near-Infrared-Emissive Coordination Polymer Glass
items.abstract: Meltable coordination polymers (CPs) combine liquid-phase processability with the structural and functional diversity of crystalline coordination compounds, but methods to install targeted local coordination environments and photophysical functions in CP glasses remain limited. Here, we demonstrate that 1,10-phenanthroline (phen) reacts with the 1D-extended Cu I -CP Cu(ipim) (Cuip; ipim − = 2-isopropylimidazolate) in the melt, converting half of the linearly coordinated Cu I sites into pseudo-tetrahedral [Cu(phen)(ipim) 2 ] − units while preserving chain topology and the interchain-separation melting mechanism. Depending on thermal history, the resulting phen 0.5 Cuip forms either a melt-quenched glass or crystalline polymorphs, whereas pristine Cuip invariably recrystallizes on cooling. X-ray total scattering and spectroscopic analyses show that the local Cu I -phen motif is retained across the phases, while the coordination geometry, interchain order, and phen···phen π-stacking interactions differ. items.title: Effects due to the solvent density distribution on the dynamics of polymer coils in solution under rheological flow fields
items.abstract: We study the behaviour of highly resolved polymer chains under rheological flow fields encompassing varying levels of hydrodynamic interactions (HI) using dissipative particle dynamics (DPD) simulations. The chains are discretized to a single Kuhn step, while the spring lengths set the level of HI. While the overall trends agree with Brownian dynamics (BD) simulations of similarly resolved chains, the balance of drag and restoring spring forces is unable to explain the chain stretch obtained for DPD simulations with higher HI (lower spring length) at moderately large flow rates. For compact coils showing high levels of HI in DPD simulations, the solvent density remains low deep inside the coil, which persists to some extent even as the chains stretch at higher flow rates. In contrast, the solvent density remains nearly constant, at the bulk value, across expanded coils with larger spring lengths. We show how this density distribution has implications for the viscosity of the interface between the polymer coil and solvent and provides a correction to the viscosity used in the drag force expression, which explains the chain stretch values observed in simulations. items.title: Unlocking Ligand-Centered Redox Activity in an Indenyl Framework through Phosphorus Substitution
items.abstract: Herein, we show that a phosphonium-substituted diphosphaindenylide (PPIPh) functions as a genuine two-electron redox-active π-ligand. The cationic manganese complex [Mn(CO)3(η5‑PPIPh)][BArF24] ([1][BArF24]) undergoes a reversible two-electron reduction to afford the isolable anionic complex [K(18c6)][Mn(CO)3(η3‑PPIPh)]·([K(18c6)][BArF24])n (n = 1 – 5). This constitutes the first isolable and structurally characterized two-electron redox couple of an indenyl-derived manganese complex, which has previously eluded isolation with purely carbocyclic indenyl ligands. Computational studies establish manganese in the +I oxidation state in both complexes, demonstrating that the redox process is exclusively ligand-centered. The redox-activity of the ligand also translates into chemical reactivity, with the anionic complex affording 91% yield in the hydroboration of 2-acetonaphthone, compared to only 7% for [1][BArF24].

items.abstract: The evolution of small interfering RNA (siRNA) therapeutics toward increasingly complex chemical architecture has created analytical challenges for structural characterization. Confident sequencing and site-specific localization of modifications by tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) remain difficult due to non-canonical backbone chemistry, diverse chemical modifications and attached conjugates, all contributing to heterogeneous fragmentation. We present an ion-pair-free hydrophilic interaction liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (HILIC–MS/MS) workflow that enables non-denaturing and denaturing analysis of conjugated, heavily modified siRNA constructs through temperature-controlled separation. Under non-denaturing conditions, duplexes can be evaluated to assess therapeutic integrity and stability, whereas elevated temperatures achieve duplex dissociation, permitting chromatographic separation and MS/MS analysis of sense and antisense strands. items.title: Impact of SEI Formation History on Lithium Metal Electrode Stability at Elevated Temperatures
items.abstract: Solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) is critical for stabilizing lithium metal anodes, yet its evolution under thermal stress and the role of its formation history remain poorly understood. Here, lithium plating and stripping on Cu electrodes were investigated in 1.0 and 5.0 M lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (LiFSI)/propylene carbonate electrolytes at 25 and 80 °C using electrochemical measurements, Raman spectroscopy, hard X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (HAXPES), and X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS). Raman spectra showed that the bulk solvation structure changed little with temperature, whereas HAXPES and XAS revealed that elevated temperature accelerated LiFSI decomposition, inorganic enrichment, and SEI growth, leading to increased interfacial resistance and unstable cycling. Electronic-structure calculations showed that increasing LiFSI concentration enhanced the FSI− contribution to the lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO), while elevated temperature lowered FSI−-derived unoccupied states, favoring anion reduction. items.title: BigMixSolDB: Extraction of a solubility database in solvent mixtures with an uncertainty-quantified large language model-based pipeline
items.abstract: The rapidly expanding body of chemical literature contains physical data scattered across unstructured text and complex tables in thousands of publications. Translating this information into machine-readable formats is essential for training data-driven chemical models. The lack of uncertainty quantification in computationally extracted datasets makes manual extraction and curation still necessary. We here address this challenge and present an uncertainty-quantified data extraction pipeline. Our fully automated pipeline utilizes large language models (LLMs) to extract complex tabular and textual chemical data directly from scientific PDFs. We systematically assess several modern LLMs and document-to-text conversion frameworks. We benchmark the uncertainty in extracted data by comparison of our computationally extracted databases with large, existing databases on solubility that are manually curated. Our pipeline achieves between 93 and 79% of the literature contained data, with near-zero median log deviations for structurally matched rows and residual high-magnitude errors concentrated in a small subset of OCR, table-structure, unit-scaling, or reference-dataset discrepancies. items.title: Evolution of primary loops in vitrimers
items.abstract: Covalent adaptable networks (CANs) comprise dynamic covalent bonds that allow topological reconfiguration. While this behavior underlies the reprocessability and recyclability of CANs, its influence on network topology, including defects, remains poorly understood. Prior simulations and indirect experimental studies suggest that dynamic exchange decreases the prevalence of primary loops, but direct experimental quantification has remained elusive. Here we use network disassembly spectrometry (NDS) to directly measure topological evolution during dynamic exchange. Surprisingly, activation of exchange at constant composition reveals two distinct concentration-dependent regimes. At concentrations above ~0.2 M, primary loops decrease upon activating exchange, whereas at lower concentrations, loop content increases, leading to gel-sol transitions. Temperature-dependent experiments and coarse-grained simulations suggest that these trends arise from competing entropic contributions that favor either loop formation or consumption depending on concentration. items.title: Environmental benefits and trade-offs of dry coating for battery electrode production
items.abstract: Dry coating is an emerging, scalable alternative to traditional slurry coating for manufacturing lithium-ion battery electrodes. It offers significant energy savings, eliminates the need for toxic solvents, and is consequently often regarded as an environmentally more benign process. Dry coating exploits the fibrillating properties of polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE), substituting the polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) binder employed in slurry coating. As replacing slurry coating with dry coating involves different production processes and materials, a comprehensive life cycle assessment (LCA) study was performed for an accurate comparison of the environmental impacts. The results of our LCA show that dry coating has the potential to reduce environmental impacts across all assessed impact categories except for the ozone depletion potential, which increases by a factor of 1.8 when PVDF is replaced by an equal mass of PTFE. For LiNi 0.8 Mn 0.1 Co 0.1 O₂ (NMC811) cathodes, dry coating typically enables a reduction in binder content by a factor of two, which offsets the higher ozone depletion potential of PTFE with respect to PVDF and results in a comparable impact at cell level. items.title: High-pressure allotropes of tellurium: Evolutionary structure prediction
items.abstract: The high-pressure structural evolution of elemental tellurium in the 30–400 GPa range has been systematically investigated using the USPEX evolutionary algorithm combined with first-principles density functional theory calculations. The constructed enthalpy–pressure diagram reveals a previously unresolved phase transition sequence Im-3m → I4/mmm (P63/mmc) → Fm-3m that reconciles long-standing discrepancies in the literature. The body-centered cubic Im-3m allotrope was identified as the thermodynamically stable ground state from 30 to 290 GPa. Above 290 GPa, it becomes energetically unfavorable, yielding to two competitive lower-symmetry structures: I4/mmm (stable) and P63/mmc (low-energy metastable). A distinct crossover occurs at 330 GPa, stabilizing the dense face-centered cubic Fm-3m allotrope. The results provide a definitive structural framework for understanding the pressure-dependent properties of tellurium, and a fertile ground for exploring the intricate interplay between crystal structure, electronic topology, and emergent quantum phenomena in elemental systems under pressure.

items.title: Digestion and Orthogonal Click Conjugation Enables Nanopore Reading of Proteins
items.abstract: Accurate characterization of bioactive peptides and proteins is needed to fully understand the origin of their activity. Nanopore reading enables polypeptide characterization at the single-molecule level. Here we describe a digestion-ligation method based on readily available reagents and benchtop equipment to convert peptides and proteins into DNA-peptide-DNA conjugates that can be analyzed by nanopores. Chymotrypsin digestion yields peptide fragments with C-terminal tyrosine residues suitable for oxidation-induced click chemistry. Subsequent selective installation of an azide on the N terminus enables installation of a template DNA strand needed for nanopore reading. The findings provide a facile approach to prepare DNA-peptide-DNA conjugates that has great potential for applicability to nanopore reading of many proteins.

items.title: Investigating Segregation Effects in Mixture Adsorption in Mordenite Zeolite Using Monte-Carlo Simulations
items.abstract: Configurational-Bias Monte Carlo (CBMC) simulations have been used to investigate segregation effects for adsorption of CO2(1)/CH4(2) and CO2(1)/C3H8(2) mixtures in Mordenite (MOR) zeolite. The segregation effects originate from the preferential location of CO2 in the 8-ring side pockets, and C3H8 in the 12-ring 1D channels; the CH4 molecules locate at both these sites. The segregated nature of mixture adsorption causes the quantitative failure of the Ideal Adsorbed Solution Theory (IAST) that mandates a uniform distribution of guest adsorbates in the zeolite framework. For CO2(1)/C3H8(2) mixtures, thermodynamic non-idealities cause selectivity reversals and azeotropic adsorption. Quantitative match with CBMC data is achieved by introduction of activity coefficients and use of the Real Adsorbed Solution Theory (RAST). The experimental data of Talu and Zwiebel (A.I.Ch.E.J. 32, 1263-1276, 1986) for CO2/C3H8 mixture adsorption in H-MOR are in remarkable agreement with the corresponding CBMC simulation data. items.title: PORMAKE2: Topology-Based Generation of Hypothetical Metal-Organic Frameworks through Single-Metal Nodes and Symmetry-Aware Linker Rotation
items.abstract: Topology-based hypothetical metal–organic framework (MOF) generators enable scalable exploration of chemical space beyond experimentally reported structures, but their accessible design space is constrained by the building blocks and assembly rules they encode. Here, we present PORMAKE2, an upgraded topology-based hypothetical MOF generator designed to improve both access to small-pore structures and geometric fidelity. PORMAKE2 introduces an expanded buildingblock library, including single-metal nodes, and implements symmetry-aware linker rotation for higher-fidelity framework assembly. These upgrades substantially expand the accessible small-pore MOF space and enable MOF designs that were inaccessible to earlier workflows, including ZIF-type and CALF-20-like structures with improved geometrical agreement. Carbon dioxide direct air capture (DAC) and Xenon/Krypton separation are included as case studies demonstrating that improved generator framework can influence downstream screening outcomes. These results establish PORMAKE2 as a more expressive and chemically faithful front-end platform for hypothetical MOF generation.

items.abstract: Bioorthogonal pretargeting offers a modular approach to targeted photodynamic therapy (PDT), but its advantages over conventional ligand-photosensitizer conjugates remain insufficiently explored. Here, we aimed to directly compare preformed biotin-containing conjugates with sequential biotin-mediated bioorthogonal delivery. DFT calculations were used to guide the design of new tetrazine dienes with tuned electronic properties for inverse-electron-demand Diels-Alder (IEDDA) chemistry. The selected tetrazines were synthesized and paired with BCN- and s-TCO-functionalized chlorin photosensitizers, and their reactivity was characterized by second-order rate constants and photophysical measurements. In vitro, sequential pretargeting produced substantially higher intracellular fluorescence than administration of preformed 1:1 ligation products; however, this advantage did not translate into enhanced photodynamic activity. Moreover, neither accumulation nor PDT efficacy consistently correlated with SLC5A6 expression in SMVT-high SK-BR-3 versus SMVT-low MDA-MB-231 cells. items.title: A Metallic Ground State in a Niobium-Pyrazine Coordination Framework
items.abstract: Conductive metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) based on low-valent heavy transition metals remain largely unexplored despite the strong metal-ligand covalency and extended orbitals that should favor electronic delocalization. Herein, we report Nb(pyz) 2 Cl 2 (pyz = pyrazine), a layered coordination framework with a metallic electronic ground state. Although charge transport in pressed pellets is limited by thermally activated grain-boundary hopping, the high room-temperature conductivity of 1.2 S cm⁻ 1 , temperature-independent Pauli susceptibility, finite Sommerfeld coefficient (g = 14.0(5) mJ K⁻ 2 mol⁻ 1 ), Wilson ratio close to unity, and periodic density functional theory calculations consistently demonstrate a finite density of states at the Fermi level. X-ray absorption spectroscopy further reveals a strongly delocalized electronic structure involving mixed Nb 4d, Cl 3p, and pyz p* states. These results identify low-valent early-4d ions as promising components for electronically delocalized coordination solids and extend metallic metal-organic frameworks beyond the 3d transition-metal series.

items.title: Performance of Highly Coarse-Grained Chain Models with Extremal Measures for a Configuration-Dependent Hydrodynamic Diameter in Rheological Flow Fields
items.abstract: In the presence of fluctuating hydrodynamic interactions (HI), coarse-grained beadspring models are known to show large deviations in rheological predictions relative to finely resolved chain models. In a recent study, we formulated a modified bead-spring approach where the bead hydrodynamic diameter increases proportionally to the mean spring stretch. Significant improvements were observed in the resulting predictions for rheological flow fields for models with many springs. In the new approach, a balanced accuracy across flow types was obtained with the harmonic mean strategy to obtain the mean stretch. In this study, we explore the limits of this approach with highly coarse-grained models consisting of very few springs. Additionally, we test the behavior of two extremal measures to set the bead hydrodynamic diameter. Note, due to the computational complexity with HI, minimizing the number of beads is highly preferable for any application. Surprisingly, our results show the validity of the approach for high degrees of coarse-graining up to only 3 springs, even with the extremal measures, particularly for extensional flows. items.title: Conformal Prediction and Multi-Ensemble Gradient Boosting for Subtype-Selective Binding Affinity Estimation Across Human Adenosine Receptors
items.abstract: Subtype selectivity across human adenosine GPCRs remains an intractable medicinal chemistry challenge. The four orthosteric binding pockets share over 70% sequence homology across transmembrane helices III, V, VI, and VII. Consequently, standard QSAR models fail prospectively. They suffer from systemic scaffold leakage, overestimating held-out affinity while producing point estimates that lack calibrated error bars. We built an open-source, leak-free computational platform to solve both failure modes. The architecture combines XGBoost gradient boosting with MAPIE Jackknife+ cross-conformal prediction, Random Forest, and LightGBM, trained on 9,589 curated ChEMBL v34 and GPCRdb bioactivity records. Under strict Bemis-Murcko scaffold partitioning (N_train = 6,332; N_test = 1,583), the ensemble achieved an overall R2 of 0.693 and MAE of 0.390 pChEMBL units. On active compounds alone (N_test = 3,771, structural decoys removed), accuracy reached an overall R2 of 0.865 and MAE of 0.314. Per-subtype R2 values reached 0.753 for A1, 0.884 for A2A, 0.912 for A2B, and 0.886 for A3. Conformal intervals delivered 85.80% empirical coverage at a 90% nominal confidence level. items.title: Olympic-patterned pentaboron emitter featuring highly distorted geometry enables efficient solution-processed ultrapure green OLEDs
items.abstract: Efficient, ultrapure green organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) fabricated via wet processing are crucial for ultrahigh definition displays but remain highly challenging due to the paucity of suitable emitters. Herein, we developed Oly-BN, a novel multipleresonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR-TADF) emitter featuring a distinct Olympic-patterned boron-distribution. The zigzag doped heteroatom polycyclic aromatic framework enables near-degenerate singlet/triplet excited states. Integrating para-N-π-B motifs helps regulate the triplet manifold and emission color point, enabling energetically accessible higher lying triplet excited states with enhanced spinorbit coupling, while also suppressing low-frequency structural relaxation and modulating the optical bandgap. Oly-BN in toluene exhibits vivid green emission at 522 nm with a narrow full width at half maximum (FWHM) of 17 nm, a photoluminescence quantum yield of 95%, and a fast reverse intersystem crossing rate constant of 6.9×106 s−1. items.title: Paving the Way Towards a Compact Complete Chiroptical Toolbox
items.abstract: Circularly polarised luminescence (CPL) spectroscopy is a technique with applications in materials chemistry, bioimaging, probing fundamental chirality, but conventional photo-elastic modulator CPL instruments remain bulky, expensive and slow. We report a compact single-channel CPL (SC-CPL) spectrometer that alternates left-and righthanded emission through a piezo-actuated pair of orthogonally aligned achromatic quarter-wave plates using a rapid CCD detector. This design minimises moving optics and eliminates the need for detector matching and pre-calibration. It can operate in various acquisition modes such as time gated acquisition mode for long-lived CPL emission and a quasi-continuous mode for short-lived CPL emission. Validation against a benchmark PEM-CPL system using a range of CPL emitters reproduced fine CPL resolution with high sensitivity, orders of magnitude faster. This blueprint SC-CPL reported herein paves the way towards the world's first complete compact chiroptical toolbox. This could lead to significant advancements with pivotal scientific and societal impact.

items.title: A Bipolar Redox Metal-Organic Framework for Metal-Conversion-Free Symmetric Halide-Ion Batteries
items.abstract: Rechargeable batteries predominantly rely on cation intercalation or metal conversion reactions, which often suffer from structural degradation, limited reversibility, and safety concerns. We report a symmetric halide-ion battery based on a bipolar redox metal-organic framework (MOF), in which energy storage is governed by reversible intraframework halogenation rather than metal--halide conversion chemistry. The bipolar redox chemistry of the μ 3 -oxo-bridged trinuclear copper centres in the MOF enables reversible halogenation and dehalogenation, allowing identical electrodes consisting of MOF microcrystals embedded within binder-free carbon nanotube (CNT) films to function as either cathode or anode depending on the halide species involved. Operando Raman spectroelectrochemistry reveals the underlying redox mechanism, while density-functional theory (DFT) suggests a thermodynamic preference for bromination over chlorination, rationalising the framework's dual functionality. items.title: What actually moves virtual screening performance: two measured resolution limits and six pre-registered interventions
items.abstract: Reported improvements to structure-based virtual screening are usually differences in AUROC or enrichment between two protocols on one benchmark. We asked what a benchmark of typical size can actually resolve, and then measured six interventions against that limit with the reading rule for each committed to version control before the data existed. Two limits, not one. Scoring the same Vina poses with a second implementation of the same scoring function — agreeing at r = 0.970, no compound differing by more than 2 kcal/mol — moves AUROC by 0.020 [95% CI 0.011, 0.029]. Re-running the whole protocol at a different search effort and scoring it the same way moves AUROC by 0.039 [0.024, 0.056]. The first bounds a comparison of scoring functions on fixed poses; the second bounds a comparison of protocols, which is what most published improvements are. Both fall inside the range in which docking improvements are typically reported. items.abstract: Despite advances in ultrasound-based noninvasive hepatic steatosis quantification, current methods remain insensitive to the microstructural phenotype of lipid accumulation, which influences outcomes in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. A methodology is introduced to generate tissue-mimicking phantom models that replicate the lobular liver histologic structure and pathologic patterns of steatosis. Phantoms consist of packed alginate capsules that mimic liver lobules and maintain continuous inter-capsule contact, embedded in agar. Lipid microparticles of controlled size and concentration are encapsulated within these capsules together with perfluorooctyl bromide microparticles serving as background scatterers. This architecture enables control of microscopic features (lipid vacuole size and density) and macroscopic organization (lobular-scale heterogeneity), both of which are expected to influence quantitative acoustic measurements, thereby more closely reproducing the histologic structure and acoustic behavior of healthy and diseased liver tissue.
