items.title: Non-bridging oxygen as the master variable linking structure to the elastic, electronic, and photonic properties of heavy, polarizable cesium silicate glasses
items.abstract: Cesium silicate glasses, (Cs2O)x(SiO2)1−x, are candidate hosts for optical, dielectric and nuclear-waste-immobilization applications, yet the large, polarizable Cs+ cation is poorly described by conventional potentials. We combine a firstprinciples reference with a single, composition-transferable machine-learned force field for the full range x = 0–0.30, built by pooling the ab initio data of all compositions with no empirical parametrization. First-principles calculations show wide-gap insulators whose gap narrows from 5.9 to 3.3 eV, while the static dielectric constant nearly doubles and the refractive index and optical basicity rise, in agreement with experiment. The pooled potential then scales these cells to nanometre-sized glasses, reproducing the density (within ∼2%, and 5% at x = 0.20), the intact SiO4 network, and the bridging-to-non-bridging-oxygen conversion and Qn depolymerization. Its elastic constants agree with Brillouinscattering experiments, and its pair-correlation functions and structure factors match the ab initio reference. items.title: Deployability-First Benchmarking of LFIA Innovation: A Framework and COVID-19 Literature Audit
items.abstract: Lateral flow immunoassays (LFIAs) are operationally simple, enabling low-barrier, decentralized testing. Their reported performance should therefore be interpreted in relation to the deployability of the required workflow. LFIA innovations often seek improved detection performance, commonly expressed as lower limits of detection (LODs), but workflows can differ substantially in burden and testing conditions. To guide experimental planning, interpretation of results, and formulation of performance claims, we developed a deployability-first benchmarking framework. At the planning stage, the intended deployment setting guides selection of a compatible workflow, while the performance question guides the type of evidence needed to address it. The framework distinguishes low-burden, enhanced lowburden, and higher-burden workflows. Once results are available, the implemented workflow, sample context, measured endpoint, LOD definition, and any comparator help determine what conclusions and comparisons are supported and how the claim should be framed. items.title: Morphology-Dependent Excited-State Dynamics in Hollow Sphere Poly(Heptazine Imide) Photocatalysts
items.abstract: Photocatalytic oxygen reduction to hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) over stable, earthabundant materials is attractive for solar energy conversion. The question how photocatalyst morphology governs photocatalytic performance remains, however, poorly understood, as the contributions of surface area and charge-carrier dynamics are convoluted. Herein, we investigate a series of hard-templated hollow potassium poly(heptazine imide) (PHI) spheres (KPHIS) with varying shell thickness and porosity. The photocatalytic H2O2 production is benchmarked against bulk KPHI and correlated with excited-state dynamics probed by steadystate and time-resolved photoluminescence and femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy under quencher-free and donor-containing conditions. Notably, whilst all KPHIS outperform bulk KPHI, the activity varies non-monotonically with shell thickness and excitation wavelength, whereby the thickest-shelled sphere ‒ not the one with the highest specific surface area and pore volume ‒ is most active at 365 and 406 nm, with apparent quantum yields up to ~3.9%. items.abstract: In recent years, the therapeutic landscape of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)–mutated non–small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) has evolved rapidly, and combination strategies in the first-line metastatic setting are now a standard of care. The FLAURA2 trial showed an improvement in median overall survival from 37.6 to 47.5 months for the combination of osimertinib plus platinum-pemetrexed compared with osimertinib monotherapy (hazard ratio [HR] for death, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.61-0.96; P = .02). The MARIPOSA trial similarly demonstrated an overall survival benefit from the combination of amivantamab and lazertinib over osimertinib monotherapy with an HR for death of 0.75 (95% CI, 0.61-0.92; P = .005), for a median overall survival not estimable yet in the combination group and 36.7 months in patients receiving osimertinib monotherapy. However, these combinations come at the cost of substantially higher rates of toxicity and a more complex treatment journey, whereas osimertinib monotherapy offers the convenience of an oral regimen and a favorable tolerability profile. items.abstract: Hans Christian Andersen’s “The Emperor’s New Clothes” endures because an entire court learned to praise what it could not see. The fable warns that when prestige, novelty, and social pressure line up together, the absence of evidence can be mistaken for evidence of excellence. In the end, it took a child, untouched by those pressures, to say plainly that the emperor was in fact naked. Prostate cancer care is unfortunately highly vulnerable to the same error. Key opinion leaders, professional societies, reimbursement incentives, and market competition all influence clinicians, and new technologies arrive from industry dressed in the language of precision, personalization, and reduced morbidity. Two studies in this issue of JAMA ask that care be judged by its evidence rather than its appearance.

items.title: “Nevus”: The Body as Text in Poetry
items.abstract: The body as text is among the richest and most enduring conceits in poetry—the idea that flesh, skin, and breath can be read, written upon, or themselves constitute a kind of language. Poets as diverse as Sappho, Walt Whitman, Pablo Neruda, Ellen Bass, and Patricia Smith have imagined the corporeal body as a form of expression or as a page upon which experience is inscribed. Physical attributes can become directions or landmarks on a map; anatomical features can be construed as metaphors; scars and wrinkles can be refigured as punctuation marks. It is unsurprising, then, that poetry written in response to medical experiences specifically should express such themes. Such is the case with “Nevus,” a poem in which the speaker sees his childhood retold in the various lesions his dermatologist assesses as she examines his skin. “She moves from mole to mole,/her dermatoscope hovering/above the surface of my pink planet,” it begins, immediately comparing the physical body with an entire world ready to be charted and read. items.title: Cortical layer 6b mediates state-dependent changes in brain activity and effects of orexin on waking and sleep
items.abstract: One of the most distinctive features of the mammalian cerebral cortex is its laminar structure. Of all cortical layers, layer 6b (L6b) is by far the least studied, despite exhibiting direct sensitivity to orexin and having widespread connectivity, suggesting an important role in regulating cortical oscillations and brain state. We performed chronic electroencephalogram (EEG) recordings in mice in which a subset of L6b neurons was conditionally ‘silenced’, during undisturbed conditions, after sleep deprivation (SD), and after intracerebroventricular (ICV) administration of orexin. While the total amount of waking and sleep or the response to SD were not altered, L6b-silenced mice showed a slowing of theta frequency (6–9 Hz) during wake and rapid eye movement (REM) sleep, and a marked reduction of total EEG power, especially in non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep. The infusion of orexin A increased wakefulness in both genotypes, but subsequent levels of EEG slow-wave activity during NREM sleep were lower in L6b-silenced animals in the occipital derivation. items.title: A simplified and highly efficient cell-free protein synthesis system for prokaryotes
items.abstract: Cell-free protein synthesis (CFPS) systems are a powerful platform with immense potential in fundamental research, biotechnology, and synthetic biology. Conventional prokaryotic CFPS systems, particularly those derived from Escherichia coli , often rely on complex reaction buffers containing up to 35 components, limiting their widespread adoption and systematic optimization. Here, we present an optimized E. coli cell-free protein synthesis ( e CFPS) system, which is significantly streamlined for high efficiency. Through systematic screening, we successfully reduced the essential core reaction components from 35 to a core set of 7. The thorough optimization of these seven key components ensured that protein expression levels were not only maintained but even substantially improved. Furthermore, we developed a much simpler procedure for preparing the bacterial cytosolic extracts, a ‘fast lysate’ protocol that eliminates the traditional time-consuming runoff and dialysis steps, thereby enhancing the overall accessibility and robustness of e CFPS. This optimized and user-friendly e CFPS efficiently synthesizes challenging proteins, including functional, self-assembling vimentin, and ac

items.title: Cellular modifiers of TDP-43 phase transition and cytoplasmic aggregation
items.abstract: RNA-binding protein TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43) can form liquid-like nuclear assemblies whose phase behavior is thought to influence its aggregation propensity and neurotoxic activity. The mechanisms that govern the liquid-to-solid phase transition of TDP-43 remain poorly defined. Here, we combined chemical and genome-wide genetic screens to identify cellular factors that modulate the phase behavior of an RNA-binding-defective TDP-43 mutant. Our screens uncovered multiple cellular processes, including RNA splicing, protein translation, proteostasis imbalance, and nuclear export as TDP-43 phase regulators. We also developed a semi-permeabilized cell system that partially recapitulates the TDP-43 phase transition in vitro, and showed that nuclear export inhibition reshapes the nuclear environment to favor RNA-dependent liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) of TDP-43, which mitigates its aggregation. Nuclear export inhibition in a brain organoid model bearing an ALS-associated mutation reduces pathogenic phospho-TDP-43 accumulation. items.title: Explainable ML force-field for evaluating protein–ligand binding energy using SO3LR
items.abstract: Accurate estimation of protein–ligand binding affinities remains central to structure-based drug design. Classical force fields neglect important quantum-mechanical effects, while quantum mechanical and semi-empirical methods remain impractical for large biomolecular systems. Machine-learned force fields (MLFFs) offer an alternative, but their performance may be inflated by training on protein–ligand complexes. Here, we introduce SO3LR-SF, a physics-based scoring function built on the pretrained SO3LR MLFF, combining an equivariant message-passing network for semi-local interactions with physically motivated terms for short-range repulsion, electrostatics, and long-range dispersion. Built on an MLFF that was not trained on protein–ligand complexes, SO3LR-SF provides a stringent test of transferability. On PLA15 (15 active-site models), SO3LR-SF attains a relative interaction error of 5.8% against DLPNO-CCSD(T) references, the lowest of all tested methods. On the FEP benchmark (8 targets, 264 ligands), SO3LR-SF achieves an average Spearman correlation of 0.51, on par with the best semi-empirical quantum-mechanical method tested (0.47, GFN-FF) and with MMGBSA (0.44), and surpassing G

items.title: Reversibility of (De)lithiation of Antiperovskite Li2FeOS through a Paracrystalline, Mixed-Valent Intermediate
items.abstract: The antiperovskite Li 2 FeOS is simultaneously cation-disordered and heteroanionic, and delivers more than one lithium per formula unit — but the structural and redox pathway behind that capacity, and the origin of its fading, remain unclear. Combining galvanostatic intermittent titration, operando X-ray diffraction and ex situ 57 Fe Mössbauer spectroscopy across the electrochemically accessible compositional range, we separate three processes: a two-phase transformation at a flat equilibrium potential of 1.95 V vs. Li/Li + , a solid solution spanning 2.30–2.55 V, and an irreversible process above 2.6 V. Delithiation proceeds with severe loss of long-range order evident by extreme broadening and attenuation of diffracted intensity. Yet, if limited to the first two processes, accounting for ca. one lithium per formula unit, the pristine crystalline reflections are recovered exactly in position and profile on relithiation, excluding amorphization and particle-size reduction. We propose a description of the intermediate as a paracrystal, retaining the parent antiperovskite topology while losing periodicity through aperiodic displacive relaxation. 57 Fe Mössbauer isomer shifts evolve c

items.title: Diffusion-Model-Guided Adaptive Sampling of Rare Conformational States in Adenylate Kinase
items.abstract: Efficiently exploring the rare conformational states of biomolecules remains a central challenge in molecular dynamics simulation. Here we show, using adenylate kinase as a methodological testbed, that the static structural scores conventionally used to prioritize diffusion-modelgenerated candidates have essentially no power to predict which candidates actually reach a kinetically rare state upon subsequent simulation (AUC = 0.500). Motivated by this finding, we introduce two adaptive strategies — direct PCA-distance targeting and replication of confirmed-hit structures — that achieve significantly higher rare-state hit rates and dwell times than extended conventional molecular dynamics or random-initialization sampling under matched computational budgets, while also enabling, for the first time, statistically stable estimation of rare-macrostate populations. These results show that structural novelty and kinetically meaningful entry into a rare state are not the same property, providing concrete design guidance for generative-model-driven adaptive sampling in other biomolecular systems.

items.title: TASTET: a Python package for geometry-driven selection of representative atomistic structures from large configurational spaces
items.abstract: Modern atomistic workflows generate large ensembles of molecular and materials structures, yet only a fraction can be evaluated using first-principles methods. Existing down-selection strategies typically rely on estimated energies, implicitly optimizing for energetic ranking rather than representative coverage of configurational space. Here, we present a geometry-based framework for representative structure selection that maximizes configurational diversity prior to electronic-structure calculations. The framework maps local chemical environments into global measures of structural similarity, which space-filling algorithms use to select diverse subsets with uniform configurational coverage. We demonstrate its performance through two case studies spanning conformational and configurational ensembles. Selecting only 3% of a 949-member Rh-complex conformer ensemble recovered the principal energetic regions of the conformational landscape, and selecting just 0.3% of 10,000 oxide-supported metal nanocluster structures likewise revealed the dominant structure–energy relationships. These results establish representative structure selection as a transferable geometry-driven strategy for m

items.title: Scaffold-Controlled Evaluation of Molecular Representations for Antimalarial Activity Prediction

items.title: Solid-State Host–Guest Chemistry of Cyanoborate-Bridged Cubane-Type Tetranuclear Ruthenium Complexes: Solvate Crystal Formation and Reversible Sorption of Volatile Organic Compounds
items.abstract: Small-molecule sorption by porous metal–organic frameworks has attracted considerable attention but remains largely unexplored in nonporous crystals composed of discrete metal complexes. Here, we report cyanoborate-bridged cubane-type tetranuclear ruthenium complexes, [Ru4(Cp)4{BR(CN)3}4] (R = F (1), Me (2), H (3)), as nonporous adaptive crystalline hosts for volatile organic compounds (VOCs). Recrystallization of 1 from solvents with widely varying polarities, sizes, and shapes afforded solvate crystals containing one to three guest molecules per cubane unit. The guest molecules were accommodated around the shallow concave faces of the cubane units, and the packing structures were classified into three types largely governed by guest size and shape. The desolvated solid of 1 reversibly sorbed various VOC vapors, with the sorption amounts largely consistent with the solvent contents of the corresponding solvate crystals, indicating guest-dependent rearrangement of the intermolecular packing. Complexes 2 and 3 exhibited substituent-dependent CH2Cl2 sorption–desorption behavior. Although 1 showed only very limited N₂ and H₂ uptake at 77 K, it exhibited appreciable low-temperature CO2
items.authors: Ryota Inoue, Zi Lang Goo, Kunihisa Sugimoto, Tomoyuki Mochida

items.title: Unraveling the Infra-Red Plasmons of Ferromagnetic Cobalt Nanorods with EELS
items.abstract: Localized surface plasmon resonances (LSPRs) in cobalt nanoparticles could offer a cost-effective alternative to noble metals for plasmonic applications, while leveraging their inherent magnetic and catalytic features. Yet the ferromagnetic nature of these objects and their extremely fast oxidation prevent the formation of stable colloidal dispersions, complicating conventional optical characterization in solution or thin films. To address this challenge, we employ electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) in a scanning transmission electron microscope 2 (STEM) to directly probe the plasmonic response of individual ferromagnetic cobalt nanorods. Our experimental findings, supported by numerical simulations, reveal anisotropy-driven optical modes in the infrared region, attributed to dipolar and quadrupolar resonances. This work not only demonstrates the plasmonic potential of cobalt nanostructures but also establishes EELS-STEM as a powerful tool for investigating plasmonic phenomena in magnetically active nanomaterials.
items.authors: Wajdi Chaâbani, Xiaoyan Li, Charlène Brissaud, Maria Merajoddin, Lucas V. Besteiro, Jaysen Nelayah

items.title: Electrolyte-Dependent Electrochemical Performance of a Lead-Free Semiconducting Co(II)-Halide Hybrid for Aqueous Supercapacitors
items.abstract: Developing affordable and stable electrode materials is crucial for advancing sustainable supercapacitor technologies. In this study, a lead-free Co(II)-halide hybrid material (CoTEA) was synthesized via slow evaporation and evaluated as an electrode for aqueous electrochemical energy storage. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction showed a zero-dimensional structure consisting of isolated tetrahedral units separated by tetraethylammonium cations. Morphological and spectroscopic analyses confirmed the crystalline nature and the Co(II) oxidation state of the material. Optical measurements indicated semiconducting behavior with a band gap of 3.64 eV. The electrochemical response of CoTEA was highly dependent on the electrolyte used. At 5 mV s-1, specific capacitances of 5.01, 22.24, and 21.37 F g-1 were recorded in 1 M H2SO4, 0.5 M Na2SO4, and 6 M KOH, respectively. While Na2SO4 yielded the highest capacitance at the lowest scan rate, KOH demonstrated better rate performance and lower charge-transfer resistance, suggesting more efficient interfacial kinetics. items.title: Layered Double Hydroxides with Interlayer Electrons Activate Strong Chemical Bonds
items.abstract: Layered electrides are an unusual class of materials in which excess electrons occupy interlayer regions and serve as anionic, charge-balancing species. Many prototypical layered electrides are based on subnitrides and subcarbides, motivating the search for new types of host structures. Here, we use density functional theory (DFT) to characterize a class of layered electrides derived from layered double hydroxides (LDHs). Through an anion–electron exchange process, we predict that several LDH compositions can stabilize an electride state wherein significant charge is confined in the interlayer galleries. We evaluate the thermodynamic and finite-temperature stability of the LDH electrides, demonstrating that the balance between stability and interlayer charge can be controlled through partial anion exchange. DFT calculations and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations further reveal that the interlayer electrons impart unique chemical reactivity by facilitating the activation of strong chemical bonds, such as the spontaneous dissociation of Br 2 and the reduction of CO 2 to formate.
items.authors: Yuliang Shi, Andrew S. Rosen

items.title: Connected, but for how long? A residual-lifetime criterion for the hydraulic–diffusive boundary in polyamide reverse-osmosis membranes
items.abstract: The mechanism of water transport through the polyamide active layer of reverse-osmosis membranes is again contested: a 2023 claim that transport is governed by pore flow rather than solution-diffusion reopened a debate many considered settled, and a two-phase treatment has since shown the two descriptions are not mutually exclusive once their coefficients are matched. That reconciliation, however, answers a phenomenological question, not a structural one: whether a genuine, pressure-bearing continuous water phase exists is a separate, testable claim about the material. This Perspective argues that settling it requires two conditions prior work has largely treated as one — an instantaneous through-connected topology, and its survival over the transport timescale — and that the second condition has so far been estimated the wrong way: from the total lifetime of a connectivity interval rather than the residual lifetime seen by a water molecule arriving at a random instant, the same statistical root as the inspection paradox. items.title: Fast-Response Operando Mass Spectrometry Demystifies C₂ Product Formation in Cu-Catalyzed CO and CO₂ Reduction: Burst of Ethylene Isotopologues
items.abstract: It has been a long-standing challenge in electrocatalysis to measure product formation with kinetically relevant time resolution. Here, we couple a real-time gas analyzer mass spectrometer with a modified sampling inlet to a gas diffusion electrode cell, achieving sub-second time resolution for both reactant consumption and product formation. We focus on CO 2 /CO reduction on oxide-derived Cu, motivated by the continuing interest in its reaction mechanism and its high selectivity to ethylene (C 2 H 4 ) formation. Potential step experiments for CO reduction reveal that the initial consumption of CO is fast ( 1 s), but the appearance of C 2 H 4 products can be 10 times slower, which we attribute to the time required for CO storage on the Cu surface and subsequent reconstruction into the active, C 2+ -forming, configuration. Previous studies have reported that the co-feed of 12 CO 2 / 13 CO results in the enhancement of 13 C-containing ethylene isotopologues, but the mechanism causing this remains unknown. Isotopic-labeled gas switching ( 12 CO 2 - 13 CO) experiments yield compelling evidence that 13 C species continue to exist for more than a minute at near proximity to or on the cat

items.title: ∆-Machine Learning for LC-DFT-level Excitation Energies of Bacteriochlorophyll Molecules in a LH2 Complex
items.abstract: Bacteriochlorophyll (BChl) molecules are the key pigments in the light-harvesting complex 2 (LH2) of purple bacteria, driving solar energy conversion. During this process, fluctuations in excitation energies of the pigments at ultrafast timescales, modulated by the surrounding protein environment, govern the excitation dynamics within the complex. Because of the relatively large size of these molecules with 85 atoms and their complex electronic structure, these energy fluctuations have so far been estimated using semi-empirical methods or low-level time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT). In this work, we introduce a ∆-machine learning protocol to predict excitation energies at the computationally demanding long-range-corrected (LC) TD-DFT level within a quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) framework, using a semi-empirical tight-binding analogue (TD-LC-DFTB) as a low-cost reference. Excitation energies for 7.2 million BChl geometries from trajectories of the LH2 complex of Rs. molischianum have been determined at the TD-LC-DFT level, both with and without taking the protein environment into account. items.title: Clustered Graph Partitions Provide Compact Diabatic Bases for RCI-LC-DFTB Charge-Transfer Calculations
items.abstract: Restriction-based configuration interaction long-range corrected self-consistent charge density functional tight binding (RCI-LC-DFTB) is an efficient approximate quantum chemical method that uses non-orthogonal diabatic states to describe molecular chargetransfer states. However, its practical performance depends on how the charge-localized diabatic states are selected. Here, we develop and compare two graph-based strategies for automated diabatic-basis construction: a discrete graph Fourier representation and a clustered biconnected-partition representation. Applications to benzene-assembly benchmark systems show that the discrete graph Fourier representation provides a systematic expansion that can require many diabatic states, whereas the clustered biconnected- partition representation gives a more compact and chemically interpretable basis. We further apply the clustered representation to a 16-residue aromatic oligoamide foldamer under an external electric field, demonstrating unit-resolved analysis of field-induced long-range charge localization. items.title: Unit-Cell Molecular Dynamics Framework for Cross-Linked Hydrogels: Linking Cross-Link Density, Hydration Shells, and Swelling
items.abstract: Rational design of polyacrylamide (PAAm) hydrogels involves linking local amide–water interactions to macroscopic properties. This study combines molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of “unit-cell” PAAm segments with experimental data to explore how the acrylamide (Ac) to N,N′ methylenebisacrylamide (BAc) molar ratio affects network structure and water dynamics. By modeling PAAm chains at ratios from 4:1 to 7:1, we reframe a covalently cross-linked network using a non-covalently self-assembling unitcell analogy, bridging oligomer-proxy and supramolecular modeling paradigms. Validating our findings against gravimetric swelling, FTIR, SEM, and oscillatory rheology data, we identify a two-stage assembly mechanism. Initially, amide groups undergo intrasegment electrostatic pre-organization, followed by inter-segment hydrogen-bonding.

items.title: Optical fiber chemistry for catalysis: a programmable optical fiber membrane electrode platform for reaction chemistry and engineering
items.abstract: Optical fiber chemistry (OFC) is a catalytic platform in which optical fibers actively provide photon transport, interface construction, and process control. This article develops an optical fiber membrane electrode (OFME) framework encompassing architecture, mechanisms, process intensification, and programmable control. Its anode fiber catalytic layer–ion-exchange membrane–cathode fiber catalytic layer sandwich couples internal photon transport, charge transfer, ion conduction, catalytic sites, and fluid-phase mass transport within one membrane-electrode reaction domain. Equation-driven simulations examine model consistency and reactor design trends. A normalized separation of 0.1338 gives a coplanar factor of 0.882; first-order kinetics with a rate constant of 0.0568 min−1 gives 96.69% conversion after 60 min. At a dimensionless axial attenuation of 1, double-ended illumination increases the optical uniformity index from 0.712 to 0.963; at an attenuation of 3, the corresponding values are 0.186 and 0.721. items.title: Tandem mass spectrometric analysis of interfacial lipid alkyl chains selectively modified via reactive ion deposition
items.abstract: The molecular structures of lipids, including branching, double bonds and substitution within the hydrophobic chains, are key aspects in research fields such as biomarkers and signaling, and determine cell membrane properties. Although mass spectrometry has become the dominant method for lipidomics, determining fatty acid chain structures using widely available methods (MSn via CID) remains challenging. In this study, we present reactive ion deposition as a method for chemically modifying interfacial lipids in thin layers. Highly reactive [B12I11]− anions are mass-selected and deposited onto layers containing various fatty acids, phosphatidylserines, phosphatidylcholines and triacylglycerides. Using isotope-labelled compounds, we observed that [B12I11]− selectively binds to the terminal methyl groups of fatty acid hydrophobic n-alkyl chains (≥95%). The molecular structure of the lipid remains intact during covalent binding of the reactive ion on the surface, effectively charge-tagging the lipid at the alkyl chain. items.title: Robust Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning Improves Joint Predicted-Potency and Drug-Likeness Yield in EGFR Molecule Generation
items.abstract: Optimizing a molecular generator against a single activity-model estimate can reward structures for which that estimate is unreliable. We extended our published ChemBERTa–reinforcement-learning (RL) workflow for human epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) with scaffold-separated activity modeling, empirically calibrated lower scores, bounded chemistry rewards, and matched-seed evaluation. From ChEMBL 37, we curated 6,476 unique structures with Reference/unspecified biochemical EGFR IC50 measurements; 4,491, 680, and 1,305 structures were assigned to scaffold-disjoint training, calibration, and test sets. The random-forest reward model achieved a test mean absolute error of 0.610 pIC50 units and R2 = 0.615. Uniform or potency-enriched masked-language-model continuation was crossed with three RL rewards, with three seeds and 600 generation attempts per combination. The locked LCB-versus-mean-only comparison changed GNN potency-screen yield by +0.28 percentage points (95% descriptive t interval,-1.10 to +1.66) across three seed-cluster means. items.title: Reversible CO2 Concentration in the Electrical Double Layer in the Absence of (Bi)carbonate
items.abstract: The behaviour of CO 2 at electrode-electrolyte interfaces is key in the development of climate change mitigation technologies, such as electrochemical CO 2 capture and conversion. In particular, electrochemical CO 2 capture using supercapacitors, an approach known as supercapacitive swing adsorption (SSA), utilises the charging and discharging of supercapacitor devices to reversibly and selectively adsorb CO 2 . As supercapacitive charging incurs low energy losses and can be carried out under ambient conditions, this method has the potential to achieve higher energy efficiencies than other CO 2 capture techniques. However, the design of SSA systems has been hindered by a lack of understanding of the underlying mechanism. In particular, the contributions of different CO 2 -related species—molecular CO 2 , carbonate, and bicarbonate—to SSA remain poorly understood. In this work, the role of molecular CO 2 in SSA using activated carbon electrodes was explored in the absence of carbonate and bicarbonate ions by using an inert organic electrolyte solvent, acetonitrile. items.title: A single reference-energy outlier nearly eliminates Co–O chemistry from a generative model's training distribution
items.abstract: An element-resolved audit of 44,688 oxide structures generated by MatterGen under chemical-system conditioning revealed that the aggregate composition compliance (73.27% exact match) concealed a severe chemistry-specific failure. Cobalt was omitted from 71.27% of the structures requesting it, against 8.12 ± 3.28% for the other 19 requested elements, and 98.17% of the cobalt omissions removed cobalt alone. Cell size, cation substitutability, stability gain and a general training-frequency effect did not account for the anomaly. Tracing the failure upstream showed that only one of the 8,924 cobalt oxides in the public Alex-MP-20 reference set passed the stability filter. The deficit was traced to a single anomalous reference-energy entry distorting the Co–O convex hull; excluding it raises the number of training-eligible cobalt oxides from 1 to 2,499. Four independent DFT calculations and the current Materials Project value agree within 0.024 eV atom-1, whereas the value implied by the released file deviates from them by 6.26 eV atom-1. items.title: Target breadth and mutation resilience in African-natural-product-inspired antimalarial chemotypes: a computational analysis
items.abstract: Can target breadth and mutation resilience be evaluated as distinct, complementary properties when prioritizing antimalarial chemotypes from African natural-product-inspired chemical space? We addressed this question by linking chemical-space expansion to target-specific docking and a per-target resistance-resilience score (RRS), while keeping computational evidence separate from biological activity. A hybrid library of 65 856 molecules, generated from 396 African natural products and 454 synthetic antimalarial compounds, yielded 19 913 computationally prioritized synthesizable leads. A 17-member polypharmacology-oriented cohort was evaluated by AutoDock Vina against PfDHFR, PfCRT, PfClpP, and PfATP4 using target-specific structural anchors. All 68 candidate–target pairs passed the geometric pose-quality criterion, with scores ranging from −7.91 kcal/mol to −4.63 kcal/mol. Per-target RRS was calculated from separate PfDHFR (N51I, C59R, S108N, I164L) and PfCRT (K76T, K76A) mutant panels, excluding non-binding wild-type targets from the denominator. items.title: Synthesis of 15N-Labelled Complex Saturated N-Heterocycles via Late-Stage Carbonyl-to-Nitrogen Swap
items.abstract: ‡Process Research and Development, Merck Co., Rahway, New Jersey 07065, United States ABSTRACT: Efficient construction of 15N-labelled complex saturated N-heterocycles remains a substantial challenge. Here we report a late-stage carbonyl-to-15N skeletal modification strategy that converts complex cyclic ketones directly into 15Nenriched saturated heterocycles. This transformation is enabled by a methylsulfonyl-based 15N-labelled azonation reagent that suppresses unwanted overoxidation without compromising the desired C-C bond cleavage pathway. The reaction exhibits a broad substrate scope and tolerates a wide range of functional groups, serving as an effective tool for late-stage skeletal modifications of complex natural products and drug-like molecules. Mechanistic insights on the sequential double C–C activation events have been elucidated by preliminary computational studies.
items.authors: Zining Zhang, Seoung-Tae Kim, Jingwei Li, Guangbin Dong

items.title: Runtime-steered ultrashort molecular dynamics enables million-pose protein–ligand screening
items.abstract: Applying molecular dynamics (MD) at discovery scale is limited by the cost of evaluating thousands to millions of candidate poses. We present a docking-to-dynamics workflow that makes MD compatible with screening-scale evaluation by applying ensembles of ultrashort trajectories (0.1–5 ns) to each pose. MD-score, a ligand-RMSD stability metric, serves as both a pose-ranking score and, with a threshold, an online stopping criterion. In a conditional six-target benchmark of 88 actives and 702 inactives, MD-score achieved a pose-aware ROC-AUC of 0.868 for the top ten poses, while broad pose and velocity sampling was more effective than extending fewer trajectories. Runtime steering scaled evaluation to 1,234,620 EGFR poses while reducing simulated time to 24% of exhaustive evaluation. A prospective Marburg virus nucleoprotein screen yielded three initial minigenome-active hits among 76 tested compounds. These results position ultrashort MD as a scalable dynamic filter between docking, data-driven prediction and higher-cost validation.

items.title: Direct-to-biology approach for the selective identification of ligands for alpha-synuclein aggregates
items.abstract: The selective targeting of α-synuclein (α-syn) aggregates represents a critical challenge for the diagnosis and treatment of Parkinson’s disease and related synucleinopathies. While several ligands have been developed for amyloid imaging, most of them lack sufficient specificity for α-syn over other amyloid fibrils. We report here a direct-to-biology (D2B) strategy to accelerate the identification of such selective ligands. A library of 384 piperazine-derived compounds was synthesized in a plate-based format and screened to evaluate their affinity for α-syn pathogenic aggregates compared to amyloid-beta 42 (Aβ42) fibrils. Nine compounds were found to bind preferentially to α-syn aggregates, three of which displayed at least a four-fold increased binding compared to Aβ42. Further validation of those molecules using in vitro α-syn fibrils enabled to determine a new potent selective binder of fibrillar α-syn with moderate affinity (181 nM). These findings validate the potential of D2B approaches to accelerate specific ligand development for pathogenic protein aggregates.

items.title: Facet Selective Adsorption and Mobility of Anthracene Based Nanocars on Gold Surfaces
items.abstract: Atomistic molecular dynamics simulations of anthracene-based nanocars (ANTH-R; R= H, Me, Cl) on Au(100) and Au(111) facets in explicit water, investigating the combined effects of facet crystallography, substituent chemistry, and solvation previously unexplored. Binding free energies reveal stronger adsorption on Au(111): ANTH-Me ANTH-Cl ANTH-H, with diffusion suppressed upto 100 fold on Au(111). Substituent chemistry influences adsorption geometry and create varied transport regimes providing design principles for nanocar motion under realistic conditions.

items.title: Quantifying the Synergistic and Antagonistic Effects of Metal–Organic Complexation on Particulate Matter Oxidative Potential via Redox Kinetics
items.abstract: Oxidative potential (OP) is an indicator of the ability of redox-active species in particulate matter (PM) to generate reactive oxygen species (ROS) via redox chemistry in lung lining fluid. Previous studies have reported synergistic and antagonistic OP effects in mixtures of metals and non-redox-active organics and attributed them to complexation-induced changes in redox potential and kinetics; however, the quantitative validity of this mechanistic hypothesis remains unclear. Here, we evaluated this hypothesis using a newly developed chemical equilibrium–kinetic DTT assay model for Fe–oxalate system. Experiments showed three distinct stages with increasing oxalate-to-Fe ratio: weak interactions at low ratios, strong antagonism at higher ratios, and strong synergy at extremely high ratios. The model successfully reproduced the weak interactions and antagonism. Fe– oxalate complexation enhanced Fe(II)-driven oxidant reduction kinetics but also shifted the Fe(III)/Fe(II) balance toward Fe(III), decreasing Fe(II) concentrations and offsetting much of the kinetic enhancement. items.title: Condition-Aware and Leakage-Resistant Machine Learning of Short-Peptide Self-Assembly Across Bulk State and Supramolecular Morphology
items.abstract: Short-peptide self-assembly is governed jointly by molecular structure and experimental environment, yet many predictive workflows treat condition-specific observations as independent samples. Here, a source-audited dataset was reconstructed from PeptideMiner and SAPdb to evaluate bulk-state and supramolecular-morphology prediction under leakage-resistant validation. Peptide identity was defined from sequence,terminal modifications,non-terminal modifications,peptide-system annotations,and conjugate partners; experimental descriptors included concentration, pH, temperature, thermal history, incubation, and explicit solvent composition. A conventional random row split was shown to be strongly non-independent: 87.3% of test molecular identities had already appeared in training and 94.2% of test rows came from molecules represented in training.Accordingly,all primary claims were based on molecular-identity-grouped validation and permanently sealed holdouts containing previously unseen molecular systems. For hydrogel versus non-gel prediction, a tuned Random Forest achieved ROCAUC 0.977, PR-AUC 0.882, balanced accuracy 0.945, F1 0.880, and MCC 0.836 on 115 conditions from 20 unseen mole

items.title: Chemically Fueled Spatiotemporal Patterns from Charge-transfer Supramolecular Assembly
items.abstract: Creating synthetic systems that autonomously form complex patterns remains a frontier challenge in chemistry and materials science. Here, we present a redox-responsive supramolecular system in which coupled changes in chemical state, assembly, and transport generate spatiotemporal patterns through density-driven chemoconvection. Charge-transfer complexes of pyranine and viologen derivatives undergo reversible redox-controlled assembly–disassembly cycles, producing composition-dependent buoyancy that drive convective flows and feeds back into the evolving assembly distribution. Molecular amphiphilicity and supramolecular assembly morphology tune the resulting pattern type, dot-, stripe-, and flower-like structures without external fields. Finite-element simulations reproduce the observed chemoconvective dynamics, while linear stability analysis predicts the onset conditions and its characteristic wavelength. A weakly nonlinear analysis further identifies reduced translational diffusivity of elongated assemblies as a mechanism that weakens hexagonal mode selection and favors anisotropic near-onset states. These results provide a molecular-to-macroscopic framework for coupling supramo

items.title: Chainable DataFrame Framework for Interactive Chemical Data Processing with pdChemChain
items.abstract: Computational chemists frequently build data processing workflows as ad-hoc scripts that are difficult to reuse, share, or deploy. Yet, many of the alternative workflow platforms demand significant complexity overhead or create manual breaks in workflows involving different pieces of software. pdChemChain is an open-source Python framework that bridges interactive use in python with reuse and deployment, by treating chemical data processing chains as composable, self-serializing pandas DataFrame operations. The framework is built around three design principles: (1) every operation takes a DataFrame and returns a DataFrame, (2) operations compose via the + operator into chains that are themselves operations, and (3) all chains are self-configuring, i.e. serializable to YAML for command-line deployment without code changes. Chains are built interactively in notebooks with immediate visual feedback, then deployed as-is via CLI or as scoring components in generative design frameworks. Built on widely used RDKit and pandas, pdChemChain provides links for molecular processing, property calculation, score transformation, and multi-parameter aggregation, while remaining extensible through

items.title: Carbon Nanotube-Induced Magnetic Shielding Effects on 129Xe NMR from Equivariant Neural Networks
items.abstract: Equivariant graph neural networks (EGNNs) have shown success in building efficient and accurate machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) for molecular dynamics (MD) and in enabling the prediction of nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) parameters in complex systems. In this work, EGNNs are used to fine-tune an atomistic foundation model, which serves as an MLIP for large-scale molecular dynamics simulations of xenon in carbon nanotubes. In addition, EGNNs are employed to develop a machine learning model for the 129 Xe NMR magnetic shielding tensor, σ , enabling its direct prediction from MLMD snapshots. Both models are data-efficient and remain accurate well beyond their training data. Using this dual-model framework, we show that xenon encapsulated in carbon nanotubes experiences a nanotube-induced, negative 129 Xe isotropic chemical shift that varies non-monotonically with nanotube diameter and depends further on temperature and Xe loading, establishing this dual-model approach as an efficient route to interpreting confinement-driven 129 Xe NMR response.
items.authors: Ouail Zakary, Tiia Jacklin, Perttu Lantto

items.title: Operando Investigation of the Lithiation Mechanism in CsPbCl3 Perovskite
items.abstract: Metal halide perovskites offer a structurally responsive platform for lithium-ion battery components, however the interplay between structural transformation and electrochemical functionality remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the lithiation mechanism in all-inorganic CsPbCl3 perovskite as a model system for resolving electrochemically driven phase reconstruction relevant to artificial solid electrolyte interphase concepts. Operando X-ray diffraction combined with electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, reveals that lithiation proceeds via a multistep pathway initiated by irreversible perovskite decomposition, resulting in formation of metallic Pb and mixed Cs–Li–Cl phases. Subsequently, reversible alloying reactions during the first cycle leads to the emergence of Li–Pb intermetallic compounds including LiPb and Li8Pb3. The evolution of diffraction features correlates with pronounced changes in the impedance response, revealing a transition from kinetically hindered conversion to more facile charge-transfer and diffusion-associated processes during alloying. items.title: Automated Symbolic Derivation Enables Scalable Ensemble DFT for Strongly Correlated Molecules and Materials
items.abstract: Strong electron correlation governs the chemistry of bond breaking, polyradicals, and excited states, yet accurately describing it requires computational methods whose cost increases steeply with system size. We present a scalable ensemble density functional theory (eDFT) methodology that extends accurate treatment of strong correlation to molecular systems of realistic size at standard Kohn-Sham DFT cost. Automated derivation of the method’s working equations and a data-driven acceleration scheme enable linear scaling with active-space size while retaining multiconfigurational accuracy. Applied to systems inaccessible to standard Kohn-Sham DFT methods, such as multiple bond dissociation, open-shell polyradicals, and a recently synthesized magnetic quantum material, the framework reproduces experimental magnetic gaps and near-exact wavefunction benchmarks using active spaces up to ten electrons in ten orbitals, thus removing a long-standing barrier to routine simulation of strongly correlated matter.

items.title: Coupling Insoluble Pteroic Acid Using Quaternary Ammonium Salts: Synthesis of a Peptide Bearing a Folic Acid Moiety
items.abstract: Herein, I report a unique coupling method for insoluble pteroic acid. Tetraalkylammonium hydroxide effectively enabled solubilization, efficient coupling with an amine, and an easy workup process to produce folate-conjugated peptides. The generality and versatility were confirmed through coupling studies of several amino acids, demonstrating its applicability to the synthesis of various folate and pteroate conjugates.

items.title: Molarium: Agent-Generated Adaptive Software for Molecular Design
items.abstract: Commercial drug discovery software has traditionally bundled three sources of value: the interface, the scientific models, and the specialized expertise required to run the models through the interface, thereby translating outputs into design decisions. Large language models, coding agents, and tool-using agents are beginning to unbundle this paradigm. Interfaces, analyses, workflow logic, and substantial portions of scientific software can increasingly be generated to meet the needs of a particular scientist, project, and question, while agents can automate sophisticated workflows that once required specialist users. This shift repositions where competitive advantage is created in computational drug discovery. More intuitive interfaces and faster execution alone do not fix model inaccuracies or broaden the applicability domain. As the underlying tooling becomes increasingly accessible and fluid, strategic differentiation will shift away from familiarity with a particular software package and toward superior preditive algorithms, more generalizable models, proprietary experimental data, accumulated discovery intelligence, and the human discernment needed to frame the right question

items.title: Operando Cross-Sectional Nanoscale Imaging of Na Anode Formation in Zero-Excess Solid-State Batteries: Coupled Phase–Stress Evolution and X-ray Beam Effects
items.abstract: Zero-excess solid-state sodium batteries plate Na during charging, which places severe demands on the mechanical stability of the evolving anode and its interfaces. This work resolves the spatiotemporal evolution of phase formation and mechanical stresses across buried interfaces in a Na-Pb model system using a custom-built operando cell for cross-sectional X-ray nanodiffraction with a beam of 150 nm in diameter. The operando phase maps reveal that Na, Pb/NaPb3, and NaPb/Na9Pb4 phases coexist spatially during plating, contradicting the predominantly sequential pathway reported for liquid-electrolyte Na-Pb systems. The temporal evolution of the deviatoric in-plane stress reveals an increasingly compressive state within the solid-state electrolyte, concentrated near the interface and consistent with Na filling residual pores within the ceramic electrolyte, thereby creating local stress concentrations associated with dendritic growth and failure. Unexpectedly, comparison with beam-free reference cells reveals that X-ray exposure measurably suppresses Na plating, evidenced by an altered electrochemical response and substantially reduced Na and alloy formation. items.title: Reliable Structure-Processing-Performance Learning in Organic Photovoltaics: Chemical Generalization, Processing-Aware Prediction and Uncertainty under Domain Shift
items.abstract: Machine-learning models for organic photovoltaics (OPVs) can achieve strong performance under random train-test splits, but such evaluation may overstate prospective generalization when literaturederived datasets contain repeated publications and material systems. Here, two complementary OPV benchmarks were constructed to separate interpolation from chemical extrapolation: a provenanceclean OPV-DB cohort containing 21,590 experimentally reported devices and a processing-rich Wen-Zhang-Ma cohort containing 994 unique physical processing conditions. Random, publication-heldout, donor-acceptor (D:A)-pair-held-out, acceptor-held-out, and donor-held-out validation regimes were compared, together with structure-only, processing-only, and combined structure-processing representations. items.title: A Zero-Shot Single-Point Chemical Language Model Mimics Medicinal Chemist Reasoning for Molecular Optimization and STING Inhibitor Development in Alzheimer’s Disease
items.abstract: Drug development relies heavily on the ability of medicinal chemists to identify productive, localized structural modifications that improve potency, selectivity, and developability while preserving favorable features of a lead scaffold. Here, we introduce the Single-Point Chemical Language Model (SpCLM), a zero-shot molecular optimization framework designed to computationally emulate this iterative medicinal chemistry paradigm. Built on a Transformer architecture, SpCLM performs controlled single-point molecular modifications encompassing common medicinal chemistry operations and generates focused, chemically interpretable analog spaces rather than large, unconstrained molecular libraries. This strategy enables efficient exploration of structure–activity relationships while maintaining close structural relationships to experimentally tractable lead compounds. Across multiple protein targets and molecular optimization tasks, SpCLM generated compact libraries typically comprising only a few hundred molecules, yet recovered 60%–80% of experimentally validated active compounds from held-out test sets that were not included during model training. items.title: Novel green K-based Metal-Organic Framework with high proton conductivity
items.abstract: Despite growing interest in metal-organic frameworks (MOFs for protonconductivity applications, monovalent-cation-based MOFs remain comparatively underexplored due to the weaker coordination interactions typically associated with these systems. In this work, we report GR-MOF-28, a novel potassium-based naphthalene tetracarboxylate framework synthesized under mild aqueous conditions at room temperature. Structurally, GR-MOF-28 consists of K2O10 dioctahedra interconnected through tetracarboxylate ligands and coordinated water molecules, generating a confined hydrogen-bond network along the crystallographic channels. The material exhibits proton conductivity values up to 4.3·10-2 S·cm-1 under high relative humidity conditions, placing it among the highest-performing K-based MOFs reported to date. Combined electrochemical impedance spectroscopy and molecular simulations support a water-mediated Grotthusstype proton transport mechanism through the confined hydrogen-bond network. In addition, GR-MOF-28 can be incorporated into a conductive polymer matrix without loss of proton transport properties. items.title: Dynamic vacancy redistribution shifts Pd nanoparticle coalescence from orientation-gated to defect-enabled on reduced CeO2(110)
items.abstract: Sintering deactivates supported catalysts, yet how mobile support defects couple to crystallographic transport anisotropy during nanoparticle coalescence remains poorly understood. Here, we develop a ternary Ce–O–Pd machine-learning interatomic potential (Ce–O–Pd MLIP) by fine-tuning a pre-trained large atomic model and validate it against density functional theory (DFT) calculations and ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD). Large-scale deep potential molecular dynamics (DPMD) simulations resolve early-stage coarsening of Pd 62 /Pd 287 nanoparticle pairs on CeO 2–x (110) and reveal direction-selective coalescence: [11̅0]-aligned pairs exhibit higher probabilities and shorter onset times than [001]-aligned pairs. CI-NEB calculations identify complementary transport anisotropies, with Pd adatom diffusion favored along [11̅0] and oxygen-vacancy migration favored along [001], enabling dynamic defect redistribution within the interparticle region. items.title: Design and computational evaluation of reversible covalent cathepsin S inhibitors using molecular docking, ADMET, molecular dynamics, MM/PBSA, and density functional theory
items.abstract: Cathepsin S (CatS) is unique among lysosomal cathepsins in retaining significant proteolytic activity under extracellular conditions. Its extracellular activity has been implicated in tumour progression, chronic inflammation, autoimmune disorders, and cardiovascular diseases, making CatS an attractive target for the development of selective covalent inhibitors . In the present study, a series of 100 α-cyanoacrylamide derivatives was rationally designed and evaluated using computational approaches. The compounds were first assessed by rigid molecular docking. Top candidates were selected for pharmacokinetics study and initial 25 ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulations for further stability evaluation. Based on these results, Compounds F7 and F48 were subjected to density functional theory (DFT) calculations, covalent and non-covalent induced fit docking, followed by 100 ns MD simulations. Complex stability and binding behaviour were further examined using root mean square deviation (RMSD), root mean square fluctuation (RMSF), hydrogen-bond analysis, free-energy landscape analysis, per-residue energy decomposition, and molecular mechanics Poisson-Boltzman surface area (MM/PBSA) calcul
items.authors: Yousif Sajjad Hasan

items.title: Accelerated characterization of active natural extracts with single-step microfractionation coupled to mass spectrometry and bioassays
items.abstract: Microfractionation is a prominent alternative for the discovery and characterization of bioactive natural products in complex extracts (e.g., plant, fungal, or microbial); however, the method faces limitations as it requires arduous scale-up for full structural characterization of selected constituents. Furthermore, the integration of microfractionation data with metabolomic data is still a complex and tedious process. To circumvent current limitations, we developed a single-step (i.e., no gram-scale isolation or orthogonal chromatographic steps) microfractionation method that delivers 94 fractions in a 96-deep-well plate, combining biological and computational metabolomic readouts at the milligram scale. Fractionation is coupled to a single-quadrupole mass analyzer, which enables integration with high-resolution metabolomic outputs through an open-source graphical interface we developed. To illustrate the method’s performance, we applied it to characterize extracts from seven plant species — Macleaya microcarpa , Macleaya cordata , Ruta corsica, Thymus camphoratus, Helleborus foetidus, Hypericum hookerianum, and Hypericum olympicum — spanning different extract complexities and bio

items.title: A computed thermoelectric feature database for 50,992 GNoME materials
items.abstract: Machine-learning interatomic potentials now make it feasible to compute rich physical property sets for very large libraries of hypothetical crystals, but such feature sets are rarely released in analysis-ready form, and thermal-transport descriptors — central to thermoelectric performance — are especially scarce. Here we present a computed feature database for 50,992 novel, thermodynamically plausible crystalline materials drawn from Google DeepMind's Graph Networks for Materials Exploration (GNoME) database and filtered for thermoelectric relevance (non-metallic, finite band gap, energy above the Materials Project convex hull ≤ 0.05 eV/atom). For every material we provide composition and crystallographic descriptors; CHGNet universal- potential energetics, per-site magnetic moments, and a 64-dimensional learned crystal embedding; a full harmonic thermal-transport layer (elastic tensor, Debye temperature, sound velocities, and Cahill/Clarke minimum-conductivity bounds); and an anharmonic layer (Grüneisen parameter from a CHGNet equation-of-state, and a Slack-model lattice thermal conductivity). items.title: Hidden Hypoxanthine Neighborhoods in β-Guanine
items.abstract: Biogenic guanine crystals can incorporate substantial hypoxanthine (Hpx) while retaining the βguanine lattice, but whether the lattice discriminates both dopant identity and local neighborhood remains unresolved. Here, periodic DFT, site-anchored cluster cross-checks, symmetry-complete pair enumeration, and GIPAW 13C calculations connect these two levels of incorporation to experimentally testable observables. In a dry 6.25% fixed-cell model, N7H-Hpx is 21.78 kcal mol ¹ lower in electronic energy than N9H-Hpx; three cluster treatments preserve a 17.40–18.25 ⁻¹ lower in electronic energy than N9H-Hpx; three cluster treatments preserve a 17.40–18.25 kcal mol ¹ preference. items.title: On Coupled Cluster Theory and Beyond
items.abstract: Coupled cluster (CC) theory is the “gold standard” of molecular electronic structure theory, yet the full arc of the subject—from its variational origins in Hartree–Fock theory, through the exponential ansatz and its diagrammatic machinery, to its modern reformulation as a system of polynomial equations on an algebraic variety, its multireference generalizations, and its emerging reincarnation as a quantum circuit—is rarely presented as a single connected narrative. This review builds that narrative completely from first principles and carries it through to today’s research frontier. Starting from the electronic Schrödinger equation, we derive Hartree–Fock theory, second quantization, and Wick’s theorem; construct the coupled cluster singles-and-doubles (CCSD) equations via the similarity-transformed Hamiltonian; and show how these same equations reappear, verbatim, as a truncated eigenvalue problem on a projective variety generalizing the Grassmannian, with a computable CC degree controlling the number of solutions. We then develop the perturbative triples correction CCSD(T), the linear-response equationof-motion (EOM-CC) framework for excited, ionized, and electron-attached state

items.title: From Black Box to Dialogue: An MCP Server for Tanabe–Sugano Diagrams as a Reference Case for Conversational Scientific Tools
items.abstract: Interpreting the d–d electronic spectra of transition-metal complexes is a routine practice in inorganic chemistry, yet the underlying models behind such interpretations are unexpectedly challenging to operate. Rigorous treatments demand specialized software, expert parameterization, and often high-performance computing, while even the standard textbook tool for first-pass intuition takes practice to read. The Tanabe–Sugano (TS) diagram remains the most efficient method for developing that intuition, and the same ligand-field framework is foundational for more advanced spectroscopic analyses. Here we present TanabeSugano, an open-source Python solver for d2–d8 TS diagrams. It is implemented as a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, letting a language-model client act as an interactive front end that operates the solver rather than merely describing it. Through natural-language prompts, users can compute term energies, explore and compare configurations, fit measured absorption bands to extract the crystal-field strength (Dq) and Racah B, and interpret B as an indicator of metal–ligand covalency via the nephelauxetic ratio. items.title: Physical Metallurgy of Lithium and Sodium and its Role in Electrochemical Stability of Solid-State Battery Anodes
items.abstract: Alkali metal negative electrodes in solid-state batteries (SSBs) undergo mechanical deformation during cycling, for which an understanding of their physical metallurgy is critical. Here, we study the link between microstructure and plastic deformation in lithium and sodium. Grain size is controlled through deformation processing, and etching methods are developed to reveal grain boundaries, subgrain boundaries, and dislocation structures. Hall-Petch strengthening with decreasing grain size occurs in both metals. Creep rate in lithium is grain-size-independent above the subgrain size, but increases at small grain sizes where diffusional creep dominates. Oxide dispersion-strengthened behavior is observed in Li. At length scales below the subgrain size, strength increases and creep rates decrease due to dislocation starvation. Solid-state electrochemical cell tests in which lithium of differing foil thickness is stripped under pressure validates length-scale effects. Overall, this work provides a physical metallurgy framework for alkali metal deformation and offers design principles for advanced SSBs.

items.title: BetaII-spectrin gaps and patches emerge from the patterned assembly of the actin/spectrin membrane skeleton in human motor neuron axons
items.abstract: The actin/spectrin membrane-associated periodic skeleton (MPS) is a cytoskeletal structure that supports axonal integrity and function. Lower spinal motor neurons (MNs) are characterized by exceptionally long axons and are particularly susceptible to degeneration in a wide range of hereditary neuromuscular disorders, including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. Using confocal and super-resolution imaging, we characterized the spatial distribution of βII-spectrin and the assembly pattern of the MPS in human MN axons derived from induced pluripotent stem cells. We discovered a striking gap-and-patch pattern in the medial axon, where sharply demarcated βII-spectrin gaps alternate with patches containing a well-organized MPS. The pattern is acutely induced by the kinase inhibitor staurosporine and pharmacological inhibition of actin polymerization prevents patch formation, indicating a requirement for actin nucleation in MPS assembly. Our data supports a model in which spectrin incorporation into nascent MPS patches depletes neighboring regions, producing long-range gaps-and-patches patterns.

items.title: Semiclassical initial value representation in curvilinear coordinates
items.abstract: A semiclassical propagator originally defined on Euclidean space is systematically extended to general curvilinear coordinate systems. This method time-evolves nuclear wave packets on the fly in curvilinear coordinates, without prior construction of global potential energy surfaces or complicated kinetic energy operators, and enables dimensionality reduction by isolating the physically essential degrees of freedom through coordinate constraints. By propagating the dynamics in a redundant coordinate space, the coordinate singularities inherent to curvilinear systems are circumvented in a numerically robust manner. In addition, the topology of each coordinate—such as its periodicity and boundary conditions—is properly taken into account by modifying the coherent state basis of the propagator. We applied this approach to molecular motions that are difficult to describe in conventional normal coordinates—pure rotation of hydrogen and methane, ro-vibrational dynamics of hydrogen, and large-amplitude torsional motion of butane—and reproduced reference eigenenergies and the characteristic features of the corresponding spectra.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence for a Circular Solvent Economy: An Environmental Decision-Support Architecture for Sustainable Pharmaceutical Manufacturing
items.abstract: Industrial decarbonization requires integrated digital strategies that combine artificial intelligence (AI), circular economy principles, and life-cycle thinking to improve the environmental sustainability of manufacturing processes. Pharmaceutical manufacturing is particularly solvent-intensive, with organic solvents contributing substantially to material consumption, energy demand, greenhouse gas emissions, and hazardous waste generation. Although green chemistry, solvent substitution, life-cycle assessment (LCA), and digital manufacturing have advanced sustainable process design, their integration into a unified environmental decision-support architecture remains insufficiently developed. This communication presents an Artificial Intelligence for Circular Solvent Economy (AICSE) framework that connects AI-assisted prediction, digital process simulation, circular solvent management, and life-cycle sustainability assessment within a structured environmental decision-support architecture. The framework retains Process Mass Intensity (PMI), Circular Process Mass Intensity (cPMI), Global Warming Potential (GWP), and Cumulative Energy Demand (CED) as complementary sustainability indic

items.title: Observation-Guided Computation: Sequential Reobservation for Robust Chromatographic Peak Detection
items.abstract: Chromatographic peak detection is the bottom-most step of the data-processing chain, yet almost every classical detector defines its decision variables in units of signal amplitude, so those variables co-vary with baseline drift, injection amount, and detector gain, and a single-pass decision is made once against an unchanged trace. We reframe detection not as a better criterion but as a change in the computational organization of observation, and we do so in three ordered layers. Layer 1 — Observation-Guided Computation (OGC) is a sequential computational framework — an analytical data-interpretation principle rather than a new peak detector — built around the Observation Deviation (OD) measure established in our companion work13. OGC does not introduce another peak criterion or redefine OD; it embeds OD as an observation measure into an observe–detect–reconstruct–flatten–reobserve loop, so the observation condition is updated after each detected structure. Within a working window the trace is normalized to a unitless observation space, scored by OD against a single dimensionless threshold, and all final boundaries are re-anchored on the raw signal. items.title: High-Throughput Experimentation Enables the C6-Functionalisation of 1H-Indazol-3-Amines as Antitubercular Agents
items.abstract: The development of novel antitubercular drugs targeting mycobacterial thioredoxin reductase (TrxR) has previously been hampered by the synthetic intractability of promising benzisothiazole-based inhibitors. Here, we identify 6-substituted 1H-indazol-3-amine as a bioisosteric scaffold that offers a comparable binding mode and improved synthetic accessibility. To address the lack of established protocols for the derivatisation of this scaffold at the C6 Position, we carried out a high-throughput experimentation (HTE) campaign with 984 individual reactions. Through parallel screening, the reaction condition space for Suzuki-Miyaura and Buchwald-Hartwig cross-couplings was systematically mapped, identifying a set of generally applicable conditions. Biochemical evaluation of the resulting library validated the bioisosteric design, yielding several derivatives with enhanced inhibitory activity against mycobacterial TrxR, including a micromolar inhibitor. Co-crystal structures of five derivatives could be obtained. This study establishes a synthetic foundation for exploring the 1H-indazol-3-amine scaffold and demonstrates how HTE can successfully address synthetic challenges in fragment-b

items.title: Engineering Receptor-Mediated Cell-Surface Mobility with Phage-Inspired DNA Tetrapods
items.abstract: Viruses have long inspired the development of multiligand display systems that engage cell-surface receptors through strong multivalent interactions. However, considerably less attention has been devoted to recapitulating the early stages of infection, during which weak, reversible interactions promote receptor-mediated mobility across cell membranes. Bacteriophages provide a striking example of this behavior, using transient receptor interactions to move across bacterial surfaces in search of favorable binding sites. Inspired by this mechanism, we developed DNA tetrapods targeting bacterial receptors exploited by phages during adsorption and demonstrate that phage-like lateral mobility on living bacterial cells can be achieved by tuning ligand affinity, valency, and spacer length. Furthermore, this platform can be extended to mammalian systems, where the tetrapod architecture similarly governs lateral motion and cell association, enabling selective cancer-cell recognition and improved antisense oligonucleotide uptake. Together, these findings demonstrate receptor-mediated mobility as a programmable property that could be harnessed to enhance cellular targeting and cargo delivery.

items.title: A simple demonstration of the importance of purity in nanotechnology with the example of rapid syntheses of gold nanoparticles in water
items.abstract: A simple and visual demonstration of the importance of purity and the impact of impurities in nanotechnology is described. Stable colloidal gold nanoparticles are simply obtained at room temperature in seconds, adding NaBH4 to HAuCl4 in water without the need for other chemicals. By adjusting the conductivity of the water used, for example by using high purity water, tap water or mixtures of the two in different ratios, the size and stability of the nanoparticles is easily tuned. Size control is easily assessed by the color of the colloids obtained and/or by UV-vis spectroscopy. This undergraduate level demonstration suitable for a wide audience requires only very simple equipment and can be broadly implemented to illustrate the importance of controlled conditions in nanotechnology, raise awareness on the impact of impurities, but also show how to leverage on negative results to turn a drawback into a benefit. Additionally, the concept and the experimental approach proposed integrate well in other pedagogical activities and are a solid foundation to link nanotechnology to other important topics in the education of the chemical sciences.

items.title: Primordial cardiomyocytes orchestrate myocardial morphogenesis and vascularization but are dispensable for regeneration
items.abstract: The vertebrate heart is composed of heterogeneous cardiomyocyte (CM) populations; however, the roles of distinct CM subpopulations in heart development and repair remain poorly defined. Here, using single-cell RNA sequencing analysis of adult zebrafish heart, we identified a unique CM subpopulation marked by the expression of phlda2 , which is associated with anaerobic metabolism and different from mature CMs, which are enriched for oxidative phosphorylation genes. We demonstrated that phlda2 + cells constituted a primordial CM compartment localized between compact and trabecular muscles. Genetic ablation of phlda2 + CMs during development severely disrupted heart morphogenesis, leading to defective myocardial trabeculation and compaction, and impaired coronary vascularization. Surprisingly, despite their essential roles in development, the depletion of phlda2 + CMs didn’t impair myocardial restoration and revascularization following ventricular resection. We found that this was probably due to the limited regenerative capacity of the primordial CMs themselves, as they failed to regenerate after either surgical amputation or genetic ablation. items.title: Centrosome migration and apical membrane formation during epithelial polarization in MDCK cysts
items.abstract: Polarization is crucial for the proper functioning of epithelial cells. Early hallmarks include the trafficking and enrichment of polarity molecules to form the apical membrane (AM) or cell–cell junctions, and the apical positioning of the centrosome. However, the dependencies among polarity molecules, AM formation, and centrosome positioning remain poorly understood. When cultured in Matrigel, de novo polarization of a single epithelial cell is often coupled with cytokinesis. During mitotic exit, centrosomes move to the future AM site, raising questions about their role in polarization. We perturbed centrosomes and polarity regulators in Matrigel-cultured cells and manipulated polarity direction using suspension culture to examine the relationships among polarization features. Surprisingly, centrosomal microtubules may not be necessary for centrosome positioning or AM formation, but their absence reduces the efficiency of AM formation. The polarity regulator Par3, rather than AM component trafficking, influences centrosome positioning. In suspension culture, centrosomes migrate in the direction opposite to AM formation. items.title: Non-Isobaric Is Not Enough: Gap-Merge Safety for Unambiguous Peptide Readout
items.abstract: Selecting a set of non-isobaric amino acids is the standard way to guarantee unambiguous readout when peptide sequences are used to carry information. We show it is insufficient. Because tandem MS reads residues as differences between consecutive fragment masses, a single missing b/y ion merges two adjacent residues into one observed gap; if that merged gap aliases a single residue mass, the decoder does not register a dropout but emits one confident, wrong residue. Non-isobaricity cannot prevent this, because the colliding quantity is a sum rather than a residue. We formalize the missing condition—gap-merge safety, |m(a) +m(b)−m(c)| τ for all a, b, c in the alphabet—as a decidable predicate with a machine-checked soundness proof in Lean 4, and characterize the collision structure of the proteinogenic alphabet exhaustively: beyond the Leu/Ile isobar and the Gln/Lys near-isobar, exactly two summed-gap collisions exist, Gly + Gly = Asn and Gly + Ala = Gln, making glycine disproportionately expensive. items.abstract: Diatomaceous earth is widely used in pest management and other industrial applications; however, non-target ecological risks remain poorly resolved. Using a predator–prey microcosm model (Xylocoris flavipes and Tribolium castaneum), we show that diatomite nanoparticles (DNP) impact the predator primarily via trophic transfer after predators consume DNP-exposed prey. Predator mortality increased with prey pretreatment dose and was higher under trophic transfer than co-occurrence exposure, identifying food-web transfer as the dominant pathway driving predator mortality. To mitigate non-target effects while preserving pest control, we developed a double-stranded RNA (dsRNA)-loaded DNP formulation via APTES silanization and electrostatic adsorption (dsRNA@DNP). dsRNA@DNP maintained lethality against T. castaneum while significantly reducing predator mortality during trophic exposure. Release assays showed that dsRNA remained largely associated with DNP across low-ionic-strength and tested pH conditions but was substantially released under high ionic strength, consistent with reversible electrostatic association. items.title: Software Tool for Automated Kinetic Tracking in Mass Spectrometry Data
items.abstract: Time-resolved mass spectrometry produces large datasets that are challenging to organize and screen for kinetic trends. We present an open-source software tool designed for the exploratory screening and visualization of time-dependent variations in extensive series of mzML measurements. Rather than focusing on automated compound identification, the software's main purpose is to highlight and rank the signals that undergo the most significant changes over time. The software streamlines chronological file organization, replicate aggregation, and trend ranking. To demonstrate its utility, the tool was used to monitor the reaction between aniline and 1-iodobutane. Crucially, the software not only correctly identified the expected mono- and dibutyl derivatives of aniline, but it also revealed the unexpected presence of aniline dimers (m/z 183 and 185), and trimer (m/z 274), and their corresponding butylated products. The automated ranking perfectly captured the consecutive reaction profiles, showing the initial accumulation of monobutyl intermediates and their subsequent consumption into dibutyl derivatives.
